18.ar: وَمَا مَنَعَ ٱلنَّاسَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوٓا۟ إِذْ جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ رَبَّهُمْ إِلَّآ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ سُنَّةُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ قُبُلًا
18.en: And nothing has prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them and from asking forgiveness of their Lord except that there [must] befall them the [accustomed] precedent of the former peoples or that the punishment should come [directly] before them.
18.tl: wamā manaʿa l-nāsa an yu'minū idh jāahumu l-hudā wayastaghfirū rabbahum illā an tatiyahum sunnatu l-awalīna aw yatiyahumu l-ʿadhābu qubulan

tr.85: Now that guidance has come to them, what stops these people believing and asking forgiveness from their Lord before the fate of earlier peoples annihilates them or their torment confronts them?
tr.19: And naught hindereth mankind from believing when the guidance cometh unto them, and from asking forgiveness of their Lord unless (it be that they wish) that the judgment of the men of old should come upon them or (that) they should be confronted with the Doom.
tr.22: And what is there to keep back men from believing, now that Guidance has come to them, nor from praying for forgiveness from their Lord, but that (they ask that) the ways of the ancients be repeated with them, or the Wrath be brought to them face to face?
tr.203: And nothing prevents men from believing, (now) when the guidance (the Qur’ân) has come to them, and from asking Forgiveness of their Lord, except that the ways of the ancients be repeated with them (i.e. their destruction decreed by Allâh), or the torment be brought to them face to face?

18.ar: وَمَا نُرْسِلُ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ ۚ وَيُجَـٰدِلُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِٱلْبَـٰطِلِ لِيُدْحِضُوا۟ بِهِ ٱلْحَقَّ ۖ وَٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ ءَايَـٰتِى وَمَآ أُنذِرُوا۟ هُزُوًا
18.en: And We send not the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners. And those who disbelieve dispute by [using] falsehood to [attempt to] invalidate thereby the truth and have taken My verses, and that of which they are warned, in ridicule.
18.tl: wamā nur'silu l-mur'salīna illā mubashirīna wamundhirīna wayujādilu alladhīna kafarū bil-bāṭili liyud'ḥiḍū bihi l-ḥaqa wa-ittakhadhū āyātī wamā undhirū huzuwan

tr.85: We only send messengers to bring good news and to deliver warning, yet the disbelievers seek to refute the truth with false arguments and make fun of My messages and warnings.
tr.19: We send not the messengers save as bearers of good news and warners. Those who disbelieve contend with falsehood in order to refute the Truth thereby. And they take Our revelations and that wherewith they are threatened as a jest.
tr.22: We only send the messengers to give Glad Tidings and to give warnings: But the unbelievers dispute with vain argument, in order therewith to weaken the truth, and they treat My Signs as a jest, as also the fact that they are warned!
tr.203: And We send not the Messengers except as givers of glad tidings and warners. But those who disbelieve, dispute with false argument, in order to refute the truth thereby. And they treat My Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.), and that with which they are warned, as a jest and mockery!

18.ar: وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّن ذُكِّرَ بِـَٔايَـٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهَا وَنَسِىَ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ ۚ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَن يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًا ۖ وَإِن تَدْعُهُمْ إِلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ فَلَن يَهْتَدُوٓا۟ إِذًا أَبَدًا
18.en: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forth? Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if you invite them to guidance - they will never be guided, then - ever.
18.tl: waman aẓlamu mimman dhukkira biāyāti rabbihi fa-aʿraḍa ʿanhā wanasiya mā qaddamat yadāhu innā jaʿalnā ʿalā qulūbihim akinnatan an yafqahūhu wafī ādhānihim waqran wa-in tadʿuhum ilā l-hudā falan yahtadū idhan abadan

tr.85: Who could be more wrong than the person who is reminded of his Lord’s messages and turns his back on them, ignoring what his hands are storing up for him [in the Hereafter]? We have put covers over their hearts, so they cannot understand the Quran, and We put heaviness in their ears: although you call them to guidance [Prophet] they will never accept it.
tr.19: And who doth greater wrong than he who hath been reminded of the revelations of his Lord, yet turneth away from them and forgetteth what his hands send forward (to the Judgment)? Lo! on their hearts We have placed coverings so that they understand not, and in their ears a deafness. And though thou call them to the guidance, in that case they can never be led aright.
tr.22: And who doth more wrong than one who is reminded of the Signs of his Lord, but turns away from them, forgetting the (deeds) which his hands have sent forth? Verily We have set veils over their hearts lest they should understand this, and over their ears, deafness, if thou callest them to guidance, even then will they never accept guidance.
tr.203: And who does more wrong than he who is reminded of the Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) of his Lord, but turns away from them, forgetting what (deeds) his hands have sent forth. Truly, We have set veils over their hearts lest they should understand this (the Qur’ân), and in their ears, deafness. And if you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) call them to guidance, even then they will never be guided.

18.ar: وَرَبُّكَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ذُو ٱلرَّحْمَةِ ۖ لَوْ يُؤَاخِذُهُم بِمَا كَسَبُوا۟ لَعَجَّلَ لَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابَ ۚ بَل لَّهُم مَّوْعِدٌ لَّن يَجِدُوا۟ مِن دُونِهِۦ مَوْئِلًا
18.en: And your Lord is the Forgiving, the possessor of mercy. If He were to impose blame upon them for what they earned, He would have hastened for them the punishment. Rather, for them is an appointment from which they will never find an escape.
18.tl: warabbuka l-ghafūru dhū l-raḥmati law yuākhidhuhum bimā kasabū laʿajjala lahumu l-ʿadhāba bal lahum mawʿidun lan yajidū min dūnihi mawilan

tr.85: Your Lord is the Most Forgiving, and full of mercy: if He took them to task for the wrongs they have done, He would hasten their punishment on. They have an appointed time from which they will have no escape,
tr.19: Thy Lord is the Forgiver, Full of Mercy. If He took them to task (now) for what they earn, He would hasten on the doom for them; but theirs is an appointed term from which they will find no escape.
tr.22: But your Lord is Most forgiving, full of Mercy. If He were to call them (at once) to account for what they have earned, then surely He would have hastened their punishment: but they have their appointed time, beyond which they will find no refuge.
tr.203: And your Lord is Most Forgiving, Owner of Mercy. Were He to call them to account for what they have earned, then surely, He would have hastened their punishment. But they have their appointed time, beyond which they will find no escape.

18.ar: وَتِلْكَ ٱلْقُرَىٰٓ أَهْلَكْنَـٰهُمْ لَمَّا ظَلَمُوا۟ وَجَعَلْنَا لِمَهْلِكِهِم مَّوْعِدًا
18.en: And those cities - We destroyed them when they wronged, and We made for their destruction an appointed time.
18.tl: watil'ka l-qurā ahlaknāhum lammā ẓalamū wajaʿalnā limahlikihim mawʿidan

tr.85: [just like] the former communities We destroyed for doing wrong: We set an appointed time for their destruction.
tr.19: And (all) those townships! We destroyed them when they did wrong, and We appointed a fixed time for their destruction.
tr.22: Such were the populations we destroyed when they committed iniquities; but we fixed an appointed time for their destruction.
tr.203: And these towns (population, - ‘Âd, Thamûd) We destroyed them when they did wrong. And We appointed a fixed time for their destruction.

18.ar: وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِفَتَىٰهُ لَآ أَبْرَحُ حَتَّىٰٓ أَبْلُغَ مَجْمَعَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ أَوْ أَمْضِىَ حُقُبًا
18.en: And [mention] when Moses said to his boy [i.e., servant], "I will not cease [traveling] until I reach the junction of the two seas or continue for a long period."
18.tl: wa-idh qāla mūsā lifatāhu lā abraḥu ḥattā ablugha majmaʿa l-baḥrayni aw amḍiya ḥuquban

tr.85: Moses said to his servant, ‘I will not rest until I reach the place where the two seas meet, even if it takes me years!’
tr.19: And when Moses said unto his servant: I will not give up until I reach the point where the two rivers meet, though I march on for ages.
tr.22: Behold, Moses said to his attendant, "I will not give up until I reach the junction of the two seas or (until) I spend years and years in travel."
tr.203: And (remember) when Mûsâ (Moses) said to his boy-servant: "I will not give up (travelling) until I reach the junction of the two seas or (until) I spend years and years in travelling."

18.ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَا مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِمَا نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا فَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُۥ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ سَرَبًا
18.en: But when they reached the junction between them, they forgot their fish, and it took its course into the sea, slipping away.
18.tl: falammā balaghā majmaʿa baynihimā nasiyā ḥūtahumā fa-ittakhadha sabīlahu fī l-baḥri saraban

tr.85: but when they reached the place where the two seas meet, they had forgotten all about their fish, which made its way into the sea and swam away.
tr.19: And when they reached the point where the two met, they forgot their fish, and it took its way into the waters, being free.
tr.22: But when they reached the Junction, they forgot (about) their Fish, which took its course through the sea (straight) as in a tunnel.
tr.203: But when they reached the junction of the two seas, they forgot their fish, and it took its way through the sea as in a tunnel.

18.ar: فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَا قَالَ لِفَتَىٰهُ ءَاتِنَا غَدَآءَنَا لَقَدْ لَقِينَا مِن سَفَرِنَا هَـٰذَا نَصَبًا
18.en: So when they had passed beyond it, [Moses] said to his boy, "Bring us our morning meal. We have certainly suffered in this, our journey, [much] fatigue."
18.tl: falammā jāwazā qāla lifatāhu ātinā ghadāanā laqad laqīnā min safarinā hādhā naṣaban

tr.85: They journeyed on, and then Moses said to his servant, ‘Give us our lunch! This journey of ours is very tiring,’
tr.19: And when they had gone further, he said unto his servant: Bring us our breakfast. Verily we have found fatigue in this our journey.
tr.22: When they had passed on (some distance), Moses said to his attendant: "Bring us our early meal; truly we have suffered much fatigue at this (stage of) our journey."
tr.203: So when they had passed further on (beyond that fixed place), Mûsâ (Moses) said to his boy-servant: "Bring us our morning meal; truly, we have suffered much fatigue in this, our journey."

18.ar: قَالَ أَرَءَيْتَ إِذْ أَوَيْنَآ إِلَى ٱلصَّخْرَةِ فَإِنِّى نَسِيتُ ٱلْحُوتَ وَمَآ أَنسَىٰنِيهُ إِلَّا ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنُ أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُۥ ۚ وَٱتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُۥ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ عَجَبًا
18.en: He said, "Did you see when we retired to the rock? Indeed, I forgot [there] the fish. And none made me forget it except Satan - that I should mention it. And it took its course into the sea amazingly."
18.tl: qāla ara-ayta idh awaynā ilā l-ṣakhrati fa-innī nasītu l-ḥūta wamā ansānīhu illā l-shayṭānu an adhkurahu wa-ittakhadha sabīlahu fī l-baḥri ʿajaban

tr.85: and [the servant] said, ‘Remember when we were resting by the rock? I forgot the fish- Satan made me forget to pay attention to it- and it [must have] made its way into the sea.’ ‘How strange!’
tr.19: He said: Didst thou see, when we took refuge on the rock, and I forgot the fish - and none but Satan caused me to forget to mention it - it took its way into the waters by a marvel.
tr.22: He replied: "Sawest thou (what happened) when we betook ourselves to the rock? I did indeed forget (about) the Fish: none but Satan made me forget to tell (you) about it: it took its course through the sea in a marvellous way!"
tr.203: He said: "Do you remember when we betook ourselves to the rock? I indeed forgot the fish; none but Shaitân (Satan) made me forget to remember it. It took its course into the sea in a strange (way)!"

18.ar: قَالَ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنَّا نَبْغِ ۚ فَٱرْتَدَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًا
18.en: [Moses] said, "That is what we were seeking." So they returned, following their footprints.
18.tl: qāla dhālika mā kunnā nabghi fa-ir'taddā ʿalā āthārihimā qaṣaṣan

tr.85: Moses said, ‘Then that was the place we were looking for.’ So the two turned back, retraced their footsteps,
tr.19: He said: This is that which we have been seeking. So they retraced their steps again.
tr.22: Moses said: "That was what we were seeking after:" So they went back on their footsteps, following (the path they had come).
tr.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "That is what we have been seeking." So they went back retracing their footsteps.

18.ar: فَوَجَدَا عَبْدًا مِّنْ عِبَادِنَآ ءَاتَيْنَـٰهُ رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِنَا وَعَلَّمْنَـٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا عِلْمًا
18.en: And they found a servant from among Our servants [i.e., al-Khiḍr] to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him from Us a [certain] knowledge.
18.tl: fawajadā ʿabdan min ʿibādinā ātaynāhu raḥmatan min ʿindinā waʿallamnāhu min ladunnā ʿil'man

tr.85: and found one of Our servants- a man to whom We had granted Our mercy and whom We had given knowledge of Our own.
tr.19: Then found they one of Our slaves, unto whom We had given mercy from Us, and had taught him knowledge from Our presence.
tr.22: So they found one of Our servants, on whom We had bestowed Mercy from Ourselves and whom We had taught knowledge from Our own Presence.
tr.203: Then they found one of Our slaves, on whom We had bestowed mercy from Us, and whom We had taught knowledge from Us.

18.ar: قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ هَلْ أَتَّبِعُكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْدًا
18.en: Moses said to him, "May I follow you on [the condition] that you teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgement?"
18.tl: qāla lahu mūsā hal attabiʿuka ʿalā an tuʿallimani mimmā ʿullim'ta rush'dan

tr.85: Moses said to him, ‘May I follow you so that you can teach me some of the right guidance you have been taught?’
tr.19: Moses said unto him: May I follow thee, to the end that thou mayst teach me right conduct of that which thou hast been taught?
tr.22: Moses said to him: "May I follow thee, on the footing that thou teach me something of the (Higher) Truth which thou hast been taught?"
tr.203: Mûsâ (Moses) said to him (Khidr): "May I follow you so that you teach me something of that knowledge (guidance and true path) which you have been taught (by Allâh)?"

18.ar: قَالَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًا
18.en: He said, "Indeed, with me you will never be able to have patience.
18.tl: qāla innaka lan tastaṭīʿa maʿiya ṣabran

tr.85: The man said, ‘You will not be able to bear with me patiently.
tr.19: He said: Lo! thou canst not bear with me.
tr.22: (The other) said: "Verily thou wilt not be able to have patience with me!"
tr.203: He (Khidr) said: "Verily you will not be able to have patience with me!

18.ar: وَكَيْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلَىٰ مَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِۦ خُبْرًا
18.en: And how can you have patience for what you do not encompass in knowledge?"
18.tl: wakayfa taṣbiru ʿalā mā lam tuḥiṭ bihi khub'ran

tr.85: How could you be patient in matters beyond your knowledge?’
tr.19: How canst thou bear with that whereof thou canst not compass any knowledge?
tr.22: "And how canst thou have patience about things about which thy understanding is not complete?"
tr.203: "And how can you have patience about a thing which you know not?"

18.ar: قَالَ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ صَابِرًا وَلَآ أَعْصِى لَكَ أَمْرًا
18.en: [Moses] said, "You will find me, if Allāh wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in [any] order."
18.tl: qāla satajidunī in shāa l-lahu ṣābiran walā aʿṣī laka amran

tr.85: Moses said, ‘God willing, you will find me patient. I will not disobey you in any way.’
tr.19: He said: Allah willing, thou shalt find me patient and I shall not in aught gainsay thee.
tr.22: Moses said: "Thou wilt find me, if Allah so will, (truly) patient: nor shall I disobey thee in aught."
tr.203: Mûsâ (Moses) said: "If Allâh wills, you will find me patient, and I will not disobey you in aught."

18.ar: قَالَ فَإِنِ ٱتَّبَعْتَنِى فَلَا تَسْـَٔلْنِى عَن شَىْءٍ حَتَّىٰٓ أُحْدِثَ لَكَ مِنْهُ ذِكْرًا
18.en: He said, "Then if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I make to you about it mention [i.e., explanation]."
18.tl: qāla fa-ini ittabaʿtanī falā tasalnī ʿan shayin ḥattā uḥ'ditha laka min'hu dhik'ran

tr.85: The man said, ‘If you follow me then, do not query anything I do before I mention it to you myself.’
tr.19: He said: Well, if thou go with me, ask me not concerning aught till I myself make mention of it unto thee.
tr.22: The other said: "If then thou wouldst follow me, ask me no questions about anything until I myself speak to thee concerning it."
tr.203: He (Khidr) said: "Then, if you follow me, ask me not about anything till I myself mention of it to you."

18.ar: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا رَكِبَا فِى ٱلسَّفِينَةِ خَرَقَهَا ۖ قَالَ أَخَرَقْتَهَا لِتُغْرِقَ أَهْلَهَا لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْـًٔا إِمْرًا
18.en: So they set out, until when they had embarked on the ship, he [i.e., al-Khiḍr] tore it open. [Moses] said, "Have you torn it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a grave thing."
18.tl: fa-inṭalaqā ḥattā idhā rakibā fī l-safīnati kharaqahā qāla akharaqtahā litugh'riqa ahlahā laqad ji'ta shayan im'ran

tr.85: They travelled on. Later, when they got into a boat, and the man made a hole in it, Moses said, ‘How could you make a hole in it? Do you want to drown its passengers? What a strange thing to do!’
tr.19: So they twain set out till, when they were in the ship, he made a hole therein. (Moses) said: Hast thou made a hole therein to drown the folk thereof? Thou verily hast done a dreadful thing.
tr.22: So they both proceeded: until, when they were in the boat, he scuttled it. Said Moses: "Hast thou scuttled it in order to drown those in it? Truly a strange thing hast thou done!"
tr.203: So they both proceeded, till, when they embarked the ship, he (Khidr) scuttled it. Mûsâ (Moses) said: "Have you scuttled it in order to drown its people? Verily, you have committed a thing "Imr" (a Munkar - evil, bad, dreadful thing)."

18.ar: قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُلْ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًا
18.en: [Al-Khiḍr] said, "Did I not say that with me you would never be able to have patience?"
18.tl: qāla alam aqul innaka lan tastaṭīʿa maʿiya ṣabran

tr.85: He replied, ‘Did I not tell you that you would never be able to bear with me patiently?’
tr.19: He said: Did I not tell thee that thou couldst not bear with me?
tr.22: He answered: "Did I not tell thee that thou canst have no patience with me?"
tr.203: He (Khidr) said: "Did I not tell you, that you would not be able to have patience with me?"

18.ar: قَالَ لَا تُؤَاخِذْنِى بِمَا نَسِيتُ وَلَا تُرْهِقْنِى مِنْ أَمْرِى عُسْرًا
18.en: [Moses] said, "Do not blame me for what I forgot and do not overwhelm me in my matter with difficulty."
18.tl: qāla lā tuākhidh'nī bimā nasītu walā tur'hiq'nī min amrī ʿus'ran

tr.85: Moses said, ‘Forgive me for forgetting. Do not make it too hard for me to follow you.’
tr.19: (Moses) said: Be not wroth with me that I forgot, and be not hard upon me for my fault.
tr.22: Moses said: "Rebuke me not for forgetting, nor grieve me by raising difficulties in my case."
tr.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "Call me not to account for what I forgot, and be not hard upon me for my affair (with you)."

18.ar: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا لَقِيَا غُلَـٰمًا فَقَتَلَهُۥ قَالَ أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا زَكِيَّةًۢ بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ لَّقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْـًٔا نُّكْرًا
18.en: So they set out, until when they met a boy, he [i.e., al-Khiḍr] killed him. [Moses] said, "Have you killed a pure soul for other than [having killed] a soul? You have certainly done a deplorable thing."
18.tl: fa-inṭalaqā ḥattā idhā laqiyā ghulāman faqatalahu qāla aqatalta nafsan zakiyyatan bighayri nafsin laqad ji'ta shayan nuk'ran

tr.85: And so they travelled on. Then, when they met a young boy and the man killed him, Moses said, ‘How could you kill an innocent person? He has not killed anyone! What a terrible thing to do!’
tr.19: So they twain journeyed on till, when they met a lad, he slew him. (Moses) said: What! Hast thou slain an innocent soul who hath slain no man? Verily thou hast done a horrid thing.
tr.22: Then they proceeded: until, when they met a young man, he slew him. Moses said: "Hast thou slain an innocent person who had slain none? Truly a foul (unheard of) thing hast thou done!"
tr.203: Then they both proceeded, till they met a boy, and he (Khidr) killed him. Mûsâ (Moses) said: "Have you killed an innocent person who had killed none? Verily, you have committed a thing Nukr (a great Munkar - prohibited, evil, dreadful thing)!"

18.ar: ۞ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكَ إِنَّكَ لَن تَسْتَطِيعَ مَعِىَ صَبْرًا
18.en: [Al-Khiḍr] said, "Did I not tell you that with me you would never be able to have patience?"
18.tl: qāla alam aqul laka innaka lan tastaṭīʿa maʿiya ṣabran

tr.85: He replied, ‘Did I not tell you that you would never be able to bear with me patiently?’
tr.19: He said: Did I not tell thee that thou couldst not bear with me?
tr.22: He answered: "Did I not tell thee that thou canst have no patience with me?"
tr.203: (Khidr) said: "Did I not tell you that you can have no patience with me?"

18.ar: قَالَ إِن سَأَلْتُكَ عَن شَىْءٍۭ بَعْدَهَا فَلَا تُصَـٰحِبْنِى ۖ قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِن لَّدُنِّى عُذْرًا
18.en: [Moses] said, "If I should ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as a companion. You have obtained from me an excuse."
18.tl: qāla in sa-altuka ʿan shayin baʿdahā falā tuṣāḥib'nī qad balaghta min ladunnī ʿudh'ran

tr.85: Moses said, ‘From now on, if I query anything you do, banish me from your company- you have put up with enough from me.’
tr.19: (Moses) said: If I ask thee after this concerning aught, keep not company with me. Thou hast received an excuse from me.
tr.22: (Moses) said: "If ever I ask thee about anything after this, keep me not in thy company: then wouldst thou have received (full) excuse from my side."
tr.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "If I ask you anything after this, keep me not in your company, you have received an excuse from me."

18.ar: فَٱنطَلَقَا حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَتَيَآ أَهْلَ قَرْيَةٍ ٱسْتَطْعَمَآ أَهْلَهَا فَأَبَوْا۟ أَن يُضَيِّفُوهُمَا فَوَجَدَا فِيهَا جِدَارًا يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُۥ ۖ قَالَ لَوْ شِئْتَ لَتَّخَذْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا
18.en: So they set out, until when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. And they found therein a wall about to collapse, so he [i.e., al-Khiḍr] restored it. [Moses] said, "If you wished, you could have taken for it a payment."
18.tl: fa-inṭalaqā ḥattā idhā atayā ahla qaryatin is'taṭʿamā ahlahā fa-abaw an yuḍayyifūhumā fawajadā fīhā jidāran yurīdu an yanqaḍḍa fa-aqāmahu qāla law shi'ta lattakhadhta ʿalayhi ajran

tr.85: And so they travelled on. Then, when they came to a town and asked the inhabitants for food but were refused hospitality, they saw a wall there that was on the point of falling down and the man repaired it. Moses said, ‘But if you had wished you could have taken payment for doing that.’
tr.19: So they twain journeyed on till, when they came unto the folk of a certain township, they asked its folk for food, but they refused to make them guests. And they found therein a wall upon the point of falling into ruin, and he repaired it. (Moses) said: If thou hadst wished, thou couldst have taken payment for it.
tr.22: Then they proceeded: until, when they came to the inhabitants of a town, they asked them for food, but they refused them hospitality. They found there a wall on the point of falling down, but he set it up straight. (Moses) said: "If thou hadst wished, surely thou couldst have exacted some recompense for it!"
tr.203: Then they both proceeded, till, when they came to the people of a town, they asked them for food, but they refused to entertain them. Then they found therein a wall about to collapse and he (Khidr) set it up straight. [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: If you had wished, surely, you could have taken wages for it!"

18.ar: قَالَ هَـٰذَا فِرَاقُ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنِكَ ۚ سَأُنَبِّئُكَ بِتَأْوِيلِ مَا لَمْ تَسْتَطِع عَّلَيْهِ صَبْرًا
18.en: [Al-Khiḍr] said, "This is parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience.
18.tl: qāla hādhā firāqu baynī wabaynika sa-unabbi-uka bitawīli mā lam tastaṭiʿ ʿalayhi ṣabran

tr.85: He said, ‘This is where you and I part company. I will tell you the meaning of the things you could not bear with patiently:
tr.19: He said: This is the parting between thee and me! I will announce unto thee the interpretation of that thou couldst not bear with patience.
tr.22: He answered: "This is the parting between me and thee: now will I tell thee the interpretation of (those things) over which thou wast unable to hold patience.
tr.203: (Khidr) said: "This is the parting between me and you, I will tell you the interpretation of (those) things over which you were unable to hold patience.

18.ar: أَمَّا ٱلسَّفِينَةُ فَكَانَتْ لِمَسَـٰكِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ فِى ٱلْبَحْرِ فَأَرَدتُّ أَنْ أَعِيبَهَا وَكَانَ وَرَآءَهُم مَّلِكٌ يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصْبًا
18.en: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea. So I intended to cause defect in it as there was after them a king who seized every [good] ship by force.
18.tl: ammā l-safīnatu fakānat limasākīna yaʿmalūna fī l-baḥri fa-aradttu an aʿībahā wakāna warāahum malikun yakhudhu kulla safīnatin ghaṣban

tr.85: the boat belonged to some needy people who made their living from the sea and I damaged it because I knew that coming after them was a king who was seizing every [serviceable] boat by force.
tr.19: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working on the river, and I wished to mar it, for there was a king behind them who is taking every ship by force.
tr.22: "As for the boat, it belonged to certain men in dire want: they plied on the water: I but wished to render it unserviceable, for there was after them a certain king who seized on every boat by force.
tr.203: "As for the ship, it belonged to Masâkîn (poor people) working in the sea. So I wished to make a defective damage in it, as there was a king behind them who seized every ship by force.

18.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلْغُلَـٰمُ فَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤْمِنَيْنِ فَخَشِينَآ أَن يُرْهِقَهُمَا طُغْيَـٰنًا وَكُفْرًا
18.en: And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them by transgression and disbelief.
18.tl: wa-ammā l-ghulāmu fakāna abawāhu mu'minayni fakhashīnā an yur'hiqahumā ṭugh'yānan wakuf'ran

tr.85: The young boy had parents who were people of faith, and so, fearing he would trouble them through wickedness and disbelief,
tr.19: And as for the lad, his parents were believers and we feared lest he should oppress them by rebellion and disbelief.
tr.22: "As for the youth, his parents were people of Faith, and we feared that he would grieve them by obstinate rebellion and ingratitude (to Allah and man).
tr.203: "And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared lest he should oppress them by rebellion and disbelief.

18.ar: فَأَرَدْنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَهُمَا رَبُّهُمَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهُ زَكَوٰةً وَأَقْرَبَ رُحْمًا
18.en: So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer to mercy.
18.tl: fa-aradnā an yub'dilahumā rabbuhumā khayran min'hu zakatan wa-aqraba ruḥ'man

tr.85: we wished that their Lord should give them another child- purer and more compassionate- in his place.
tr.19: And we intended that their Lord should change him for them for one better in purity and nearer to mercy.
tr.22: "So we desired that their Lord would give them in exchange (a son) better in purity (of conduct) and closer in affection.
tr.203: "So we intended that their Lord should change him for them for one better in righteousness and nearer to mercy.

18.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلْجِدَارُ فَكَانَ لِغُلَـٰمَيْنِ يَتِيمَيْنِ فِى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ وَكَانَ تَحْتَهُۥ كَنزٌ لَّهُمَا وَكَانَ أَبُوهُمَا صَـٰلِحًا فَأَرَادَ رَبُّكَ أَن يَبْلُغَآ أَشُدَّهُمَا وَيَسْتَخْرِجَا كَنزَهُمَا رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ ۚ وَمَا فَعَلْتُهُۥ عَنْ أَمْرِى ۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَأْوِيلُ مَا لَمْ تَسْطِع عَّلَيْهِ صَبْرًا
18.en: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was beneath it a treasure for them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord intended that they reach maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did it not of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience."
18.tl: wa-ammā l-jidāru fakāna lighulāmayni yatīmayni fī l-madīnati wakāna taḥtahu kanzun lahumā wakāna abūhumā ṣāliḥan fa-arāda rabbuka an yablughā ashuddahumā wayastakhrijā kanzahumā raḥmatan min rabbika wamā faʿaltuhu ʿan amrī dhālika tawīlu mā lam tasṭiʿ ʿalayhi ṣabran

tr.85: The wall belonged to two young orphans in the town and there was buried treasure beneath it belonging to them. Their father had been a righteous man, so your Lord intended them to reach maturity and then dig up their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. I did not do [these things] of my own accord: these are the explanations for those things you could not bear with patience.’
tr.19: And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and there was beneath it a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous, and thy Lord intended that they should come to their full strength and should bring forth their treasure as a mercy from their Lord; and I did it not upon my own command. Such is the interpretation of that wherewith thou couldst not bear.
tr.22: "As for the wall, it belonged to two youths, orphans, in the Town; there was, beneath it, a buried treasure, to which they were entitled: their father had been a righteous man: So thy Lord desired that they should attain their age of full strength and get out their treasure - a mercy (and favour) from thy Lord. I did it not of my own accord. Such is the interpretation of (those things) over which thou wast unable to hold patience."
tr.203: "And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the town; and there was under it a treasure belonging to them; and their father was a righteous man, and your Lord intended that they should attain their age of full strength and take out their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did them not of my own accord. That is the interpretation of those (things) over which you could not hold patience."

18.ar: وَيَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَن ذِى ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ ۖ قُلْ سَأَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْهُ ذِكْرًا
18.en: And they ask you, [O Muḥammad], about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say, "I will recite to you about him a report."
18.tl: wayasalūnaka ʿan dhī l-qarnayni qul sa-atlū ʿalaykum min'hu dhik'ran

tr.85: [Prophet], they ask you about Dhu ’l-Qarnayn. Say, ‘I will tell you something about him.’
tr.19: They will ask thee of Dhu'l-Qarneyn. Say: I shall recite unto you a remembrance of him.
tr.22: They ask thee concerning Zul-qarnain. Say, "I will rehearse to you something of his story."
tr.203: And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnain. Say: "I shall recite to you something of his story."

18.ar: إِنَّا مَكَّنَّا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَءَاتَيْنَـٰهُ مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ سَبَبًا
18.en: Indeed, We established him upon the earth, and We gave him from everything a way [i.e., means].
18.tl: innā makkannā lahu fī l-arḍi waātaynāhu min kulli shayin sababan

tr.85: We established his power in the land, and gave him the means to achieve everything.
tr.19: Lo! We made him strong in the land and gave him unto every thing a road.
tr.22: Verily We established his power on earth, and We gave him the ways and the means to all ends.
tr.203: Verily, We established him in the earth, and We gave him the means of everything.

18.ar: فَأَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا
18.en: So he followed a way
18.tl: fa-atbaʿa sababan

tr.85: He travelled on a certain road;
tr.19: And he followed a road
tr.22: One (such) way he followed,
tr.203: So he followed a way.

18.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِى عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًا ۗ قُلْنَا يَـٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًا
18.en: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun [i.e., the west], he found it [as if] setting in a body of dark water, and he found near it a people. We [i.e., Allāh] said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish [them] or else adopt among them [a way of] goodness."
18.tl: ḥattā idhā balagha maghriba l-shamsi wajadahā taghrubu fī ʿaynin ḥami-atin wawajada ʿindahā qawman qul'nā yādhā l-qarnayni immā an tuʿadhiba wa-immā an tattakhidha fīhim ḥus'nan

tr.85: then, when he came to the setting of the sun, he found it [seemed to be] setting into a muddy spring. Nearby he found some people and We said, ‘Dhu ’l-Qarnayn, you may choose [which of them] to punish or show kindness to.’
tr.19: Till, when he reached the setting-place of the sun, he found it setting in a muddy spring, and found a people thereabout. We said: O Dhu'l-Qarneyn! Either punish or show them kindness.
tr.22: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it set in a spring of murky water: Near it he found a People: We said: "O Zul-qarnain! (thou hast authority,) either to punish them, or to treat them with kindness."
tr.203: Until, when he reached the setting place of the sun, he found it setting in a spring of black muddy (or hot) water. And he found near it a people. We (Allâh) said (by inspiration): "O Dhul-Qarnain! Either you punish them, or treat them with kindness."

18.ar: قَالَ أَمَّا مَن ظَلَمَ فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُۥ ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ فَيُعَذِّبُهُۥ عَذَابًا نُّكْرًا
18.en: He said, "As for one who wrongs, we will punish him. Then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment [i.e., Hellfire].
18.tl: qāla ammā man ẓalama fasawfa nuʿadhibuhu thumma yuraddu ilā rabbihi fayuʿadhibuhu ʿadhāban nuk'ran

tr.85: He answered, ‘We shall punish those who have done evil, and when they are returned to their Lord He will punish them [even more] severely,
tr.19: He said: As for him who doeth wrong, we shall punish him, and then he will be brought back unto his Lord, Who will punish him with awful punishment!
tr.22: He said: "Whoever doth wrong, him shall we punish; then shall he be sent back to his Lord; and He will punish him with a punishment unheard-of (before).
tr.203: He said: "As for him (a disbeliever in the Oneness of Allâh) who does wrong, we shall punish him, and then he will be brought back unto his Lord, Who will punish him with a terrible torment (Hell).

18.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنْ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَـٰلِحًا فَلَهُۥ جَزَآءً ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ ۖ وَسَنَقُولُ لَهُۥ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا يُسْرًا
18.en: But as for one who believes and does righteousness, he will have a reward of the best [i.e., Paradise], and we [i.e., Dhul-Qarnayn] will speak to him from our command with ease."
18.tl: wa-ammā man āmana waʿamila ṣāliḥan falahu jazāan l-ḥus'nā wasanaqūlu lahu min amrinā yus'ran

tr.85: while those who believed and did good deeds will have the best of rewards: we shall command them to do what is easy for them.’
tr.19: But as for him who believeth and doeth right, good will be his reward, and We shall speak unto him a mild command.
tr.22: "But whoever believes, and works righteousness,- he shall have a goodly reward, and easy will be his task as We order it by our Command."
tr.203: "But as for him who believes (in Allâh’s Oneness) and works righteousness, he shall have the best reward, (Paradise), and we (Dhul-Qarnain) shall speak unto him mild words (as instructions)."

18.ar: ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا
18.en: Then he followed a way
18.tl: thumma atbaʿa sababan

tr.85: He travelled on;
tr.19: Then he followed a road
tr.22: Then followed he (another) way,
tr.203: Then he followed another way,

18.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَطْلِعَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَطْلُعُ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍ لَّمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُم مِّن دُونِهَا سِتْرًا
18.en: Until, when he came to the rising of the sun [i.e., the east], he found it rising on a people for whom We had not made against it any shield.
18.tl: ḥattā idhā balagha maṭliʿa l-shamsi wajadahā taṭluʿu ʿalā qawmin lam najʿal lahum min dūnihā sit'ran

tr.85: then, when he came to the rising of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had provided no shelter from it.
tr.19: Till, when he reached the rising-place of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had appointed no shelter therefrom.
tr.22: Until, when he came to the rising of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We had provided no covering protection against the sun.
tr.203: Until, when he came to the rising place of the sun, he found it rising on a people for whom We (Allâh) had provided no shelter against the sun.

18.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ وَقَدْ أَحَطْنَا بِمَا لَدَيْهِ خُبْرًا
18.en: Thus. And We had encompassed [all] that he had in knowledge.
18.tl: kadhālika waqad aḥaṭnā bimā ladayhi khub'ran

tr.85: And so it was: We knew all about him.
tr.19: So (it was). And We knew all concerning him.
tr.22: (He left them) as they were: We completely understood what was before him.
tr.203: So (it was)! And We knew all about him (Dhul-Qarnain).

18.ar: ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا
18.en: Then he followed a way.
18.tl: thumma atbaʿa sababan

tr.85: He travelled on;
tr.19: Then he followed a road
tr.22: Then followed he (another) way,
tr.203: Then he followed (another) way,

18.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ بَيْنَ ٱلسَّدَّيْنِ وَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمَا قَوْمًا لَّا يَكَادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلًا
18.en: Until, when he reached [a pass] between two mountains, he found beside them a people who could hardly understand [his] speech.
18.tl: ḥattā idhā balagha bayna l-sadayni wajada min dūnihimā qawman lā yakādūna yafqahūna qawlan

tr.85: then, when he reached a place between two mountain barriers, he found beside them a people who could barely understand him.
tr.19: Till, when he came between the two mountains, he found upon their hither side a folk that scarce could understand a saying.
tr.22: Until, when he reached (a tract) between two mountains, he found, beneath them, a people who scarcely understood a word.
tr.203: Until, when he reached between two mountains, he found, before (near) them (those two mountains), a people who scarcely understood a word.

18.ar: قَالُوا۟ يَـٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِنَّ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ مُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَهَلْ نَجْعَلُ لَكَ خَرْجًا عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَجْعَلَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمْ سَدًّا
18.en: They said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are [great] corrupters in the land. So may we assign for you an expenditure that you might make between us and them a barrier?"
18.tl: qālū yādhā l-qarnayni inna yajūja wamajūja muf'sidūna fī l-arḍi fahal najʿalu laka kharjan ʿalā an tajʿala baynanā wabaynahum saddan

tr.85: They said, ‘Dhu ’l-Qarnayn, Gog and Magog are ruining this land. Will you build a barrier between them and us if we pay you a tribute?’
tr.19: They said: O Dhu'l-Qarneyn! Lo! Gog and Magog are spoiling the land. So may we pay thee tribute on condition that thou set a barrier between us and them?
tr.22: They said: "O Zul-qarnain! the Gog and Magog (People) do great mischief on earth: shall we then render thee tribute in order that thou mightest erect a barrier between us and them?
tr.203: They said: "O Dhul-Qarnain! Verily Ya’jûj and Ma’jûj (Gog and Magog) are doing great mischief in the land. Shall we then pay you a tribute in order that you might erect a barrier between us and them?"

18.ar: قَالَ مَا مَكَّنِّى فِيهِ رَبِّى خَيْرٌ فَأَعِينُونِى بِقُوَّةٍ أَجْعَلْ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ رَدْمًا
18.en: He said, "That in which my Lord has established me is better [than what you offer], but assist me with strength [i.e., manpower]; I will make between you and them a dam.
18.tl: qāla mā makkannī fīhi rabbī khayrun fa-aʿīnūnī biquwwatin ajʿal baynakum wabaynahum radman

tr.85: He answered, ‘The power my Lord has given me is better than any tribute, but if you lend me your strength, I will put up a fortification between you and them:
tr.19: He said: That wherein my Lord hath established me is better (than your tribute). Do but help me with strength (of men), I will set between you and them a bank.
tr.22: He said: "(The power) in which my Lord has established me is better (than tribute): Help me therefore with strength (and labour): I will erect a strong barrier between you and them:
tr.203: He said: "That (wealth, authority and power) in which my Lord had established me is better (than your tribute). So help me with strength (of men), I will erect between you and them a barrier.

18.ar: ءَاتُونِى زُبَرَ ٱلْحَدِيدِ ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا سَاوَىٰ بَيْنَ ٱلصَّدَفَيْنِ قَالَ ٱنفُخُوا۟ ۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَعَلَهُۥ نَارًا قَالَ ءَاتُونِىٓ أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْرًا
18.en: Bring me bars of iron" - until, when he had leveled [them] between the two mountain walls, he said, "Blow [with bellows]," until when he had made it [like] fire, he said, "Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper."
18.tl: ātūnī zubara l-ḥadīdi ḥattā idhā sāwā bayna l-ṣadafayni qāla unfukhū ḥattā idhā jaʿalahu nāran qāla ātūnī uf'righ ʿalayhi qiṭ'ran

tr.85: bring me lumps of iron!’ and then, when he had filled the gap between the two mountainsides [he said], ‘Work your bellows!’ and then, when he had made it glow like fire, he said, ‘Bring me molten metal to pour over it!’
tr.19: Give me pieces of iron - till, when he had levelled up (the gap) between the cliffs, he said: Blow! - till, when he had made it a fire, he said: Bring me molten copper to pour thereon.
tr.22: "Bring me blocks of iron." At length, when he had filled up the space between the two steep mountain-sides, He said, "Blow (with your bellows)" Then, when he had made it (red) as fire, he said: "Bring me, that I may pour over it, molten lead."
tr.203: "Give me pieces (blocks) of iron;" then, when he had filled up the gap between the two mountain-cliffs, he said: "Blow;" then when he had made them (red as) fire, he said: "Bring me molten copper to pour over them."

18.ar: فَمَا ٱسْطَـٰعُوٓا۟ أَن يَظْهَرُوهُ وَمَا ٱسْتَطَـٰعُوا۟ لَهُۥ نَقْبًا
18.en: So they [i.e., Gog and Magog] were unable to pass over it, nor were they able [to effect] in it any penetration.
18.tl: famā is'ṭāʿū an yaẓharūhu wamā is'taṭāʿū lahu naqban

tr.85: Their enemies could not scale the barrier, nor could they pierce it,
tr.19: And (Gog and Magog) were not able to surmount, nor could they pierce (it).
tr.22: Thus were they made powerless to scale it or to dig through it.
tr.203: So they [Ya’jûj and Ma’jûj (Gog and Magog)] could not scale it or dig through it.

18.ar: قَالَ هَـٰذَا رَحْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّى ۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ رَبِّى جَعَلَهُۥ دَكَّآءَ ۖ وَكَانَ وَعْدُ رَبِّى حَقًّا
18.en: [Dhul-Qarnayn] said, "This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes [i.e., approaches], He will make it level, and ever is the promise of my Lord true."
18.tl: qāla hādhā raḥmatun min rabbī fa-idhā jāa waʿdu rabbī jaʿalahu dakkāa wakāna waʿdu rabbī ḥaqqan

tr.85: and he said, ‘This is a mercy from my Lord. But when my Lord’s promise is fulfilled, He will raze this barrier to the ground: my Lord’s promise always comes true.’
tr.19: He said: This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord cometh to pass, He will lay it low, for the promise of my Lord is true.
tr.22: He said: "This is a mercy from my Lord: But when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will make it into dust; and the promise of my Lord is true."
tr.203: (Dhul-Qarnain) said: "This is a mercy from my Lord, but when the Promise of my Lord comes, He shall level it down to the ground. And the Promise of my Lord is ever true."

18.ar: ۞ وَتَرَكْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَمُوجُ فِى بَعْضٍ ۖ وَنُفِخَ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَجَمَعْنَـٰهُمْ جَمْعًا
18.en: And We will leave them that day surging over each other, and [then] the Horn will be blown, and We will assemble them in [one] assembly.
18.tl: wataraknā baʿḍahum yawma-idhin yamūju fī baʿḍin wanufikha fī l-ṣūri fajamaʿnāhum jamʿan

tr.85: On that Day, We shall let them surge against each other like waves and then the Trumpet will be blown and We shall gather them all together.
tr.19: And on that day we shall let some of them surge against others, and the Trumpet will be blown. Then We shall gather them together in one gathering.
tr.22: On that day We shall leave them to surge like waves on one another: the trumpet will be blown, and We shall collect them all together.
tr.203: And on that Day [i.e. the Day Ya’jûj and Ma’jûj (Gog and Magog) will come out], We shall leave them to surge like waves on one another; and the Trumpet will be blown, and We shall collect them (the creatures) all together.

18.ar: وَعَرَضْنَا جَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْكَـٰفِرِينَ عَرْضًا
18.en: And We will present Hell that Day to the disbelievers, on display -
18.tl: waʿaraḍnā jahannama yawma-idhin lil'kāfirīna ʿarḍan

tr.85: We shall show Hell to the disbelievers,
tr.19: On that day we shall present hell to the disbelievers, plain to view,
tr.22: And We shall present Hell that day for Unbelievers to see, all spread out,-
tr.203: And on that Day We shall present Hell to the disbelievers, plain to view -

18.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ كَانَتْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ فِى غِطَآءٍ عَن ذِكْرِى وَكَانُوا۟ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَمْعًا
18.en: Those whose eyes had been within a cover [removed] from My remembrance, and they were not able to hear.
18.tl: alladhīna kānat aʿyunuhum fī ghiṭāin ʿan dhik'rī wakānū lā yastaṭīʿūna samʿan

tr.85: those whose eyes were blind to My signs, those who were unable to hear.
tr.19: Those whose eyes were hoodwinked from My reminder, and who could not bear to hear.
tr.22: (Unbelievers) whose eyes had been under a veil from remembrance of Me, and who had been unable even to hear.
tr.203: (To) those whose eyes had been under a covering from My Reminder (this Qur’ân), and who could not bear to hear (it).

18.ar: أَفَحَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَن يَتَّخِذُوا۟ عِبَادِى مِن دُونِىٓ أَوْلِيَآءَ ۚ إِنَّآ أَعْتَدْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَـٰفِرِينَ نُزُلًا
18.en: Then do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants instead of Me as allies? Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a lodging.
18.tl: afaḥasiba alladhīna kafarū an yattakhidhū ʿibādī min dūnī awliyāa innā aʿtadnā jahannama lil'kāfirīna nuzulan

tr.85: Did they think that they could take My servants as masters instead of Me? We have prepared Hell as the disbelievers’ resting place.
tr.19: Do the disbelievers reckon that they can choose My bondmen as protecting friends beside Me? Lo! We have prepared hell as a welcome for the disbelievers.
tr.22: Do the Unbelievers think that they can take My servants as protectors besides Me? Verily We have prepared Hell for the Unbelievers for (their) entertainment.
tr.203: Do then those who disbelieved think that they can take My slaves [i.e., the angels, Allâh’s Messengers, ‘Îsâ (Jesus), son of Maryam (Mary)] as Auliyâ’ (lords, gods, protectors) besides Me? Verily, We have prepared Hell as an entertainment for the disbelievers (in the Oneness of Allâh - Islâmic Monotheism).

18.ar: قُلْ هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُم بِٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَـٰلًا
18.en: Say, [O Muḥammad], "Shall we [believers] inform you of the greatest losers as to [their] deeds?
18.tl: qul hal nunabbi-ukum bil-akhsarīna aʿmālan

tr.85: Say [Prophet], ‘Shall we tell you who has the most to lose by their actions,
tr.19: Say: Shall We inform you who will be the greatest losers by their works?
tr.22: Say: "Shall we tell you of those who lose most in respect of their deeds?-
tr.203: Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم): "Shall We tell you the greatest losers in respect of (their) deeds?

18.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا
18.en: [They are] those whose effort is lost in worldly life, while they think that they are doing well in work."
18.tl: alladhīna ḍalla saʿyuhum fī l-ḥayati l-dun'yā wahum yaḥsabūna annahum yuḥ'sinūna ṣun'ʿan

tr.85: whose efforts in this world are misguided, even when they think they are doing good work?
tr.19: Those whose effort goeth astray in the life of the world, and yet they reckon that they do good work.
tr.22: "Those whose efforts have been wasted in this life, while they thought that they were acquiring good by their works?"
tr.203: "Those whose efforts have been wasted in this life while they thought that they were acquiring good by their deeds.

18.ar: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَـٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ وَلِقَآئِهِۦ فَحَبِطَتْ أَعْمَـٰلُهُمْ فَلَا نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ وَزْنًا
18.en: Those are the ones who disbelieve in the verses of their Lord and in [their] meeting Him, so their deeds have become worthless; and We will not assign to them on the Day of Resurrection any weight [i.e., importance].
18.tl: ulāika alladhīna kafarū biāyāti rabbihim waliqāihi faḥabiṭat aʿmāluhum falā nuqīmu lahum yawma l-qiyāmati waznan

tr.85: It is those who disbelieve in their Lord’s messages and deny that they will meet Him.’ Their deeds come to nothing: on the Day of Resurrection We shall give them no weight.
tr.19: Those are they who disbelieve in the revelations of their Lord and in the meeting with Him. Therefor their works are vain, and on the Day of Resurrection We assign no weight to them.
tr.22: They are those who deny the Signs of their Lord and the fact of their having to meet Him (in the Hereafter): vain will be their works, nor shall We, on the Day of Judgment, give them any weight.
tr.203: "They are those who deny the Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) of their Lord and the Meeting with Him (in the Hereafter). So their works are in vain, and on the Day of Resurrection, We shall assign no weight for them.

18.ar: ذَٰلِكَ جَزَآؤُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ بِمَا كَفَرُوا۟ وَٱتَّخَذُوٓا۟ ءَايَـٰتِى وَرُسُلِى هُزُوًا
18.en: That is their recompense - Hell - for what they denied and [because] they took My signs and My messengers in ridicule.
18.tl: dhālika jazāuhum jahannamu bimā kafarū wa-ittakhadhū āyātī warusulī huzuwan

tr.85: Their recompense for having disbelieved and made fun of My messages and My messengers will be Hell.
tr.19: That is their reward: hell, because they disbelieved, and made a jest of Our revelations and Our messengers.
tr.22: That is their reward, Hell, because they rejected Faith, and took My Signs and My Messengers by way of jest.
tr.203: "That shall be their recompense, Hell; because they disbelieved and took My Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) and My Messengers by way of jest and mockery.

18.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ كَانَتْ لَهُمْ جَنَّـٰتُ ٱلْفِرْدَوْسِ نُزُلًا
18.en: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - they will have the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging,
18.tl: inna alladhīna āmanū waʿamilū l-ṣāliḥāti kānat lahum jannātu l-fir'dawsi nuzulan

tr.85: But those who believe and do good deeds will be given the Gardens of Paradise.
tr.19: Lo! those who believe and do good works, theirs are the Gardens of Paradise for welcome,
tr.22: As to those who believe and work righteous deeds, they have, for their entertainment, the Gardens of Paradise,
tr.203: "Verily those who believe (in the Oneness of Allâh - Islâmic Monotheism) and do righteous deeds, shall have the Gardens of Al-Firdaus (Paradise) for their entertainment.

18.ar: خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يَبْغُونَ عَنْهَا حِوَلًا
18.en: Wherein they abide eternally. They will not desire from it any transfer.
18.tl: khālidīna fīhā lā yabghūna ʿanhā ḥiwalan

tr.85: There they will remain, never wishing to leave.
tr.19: Wherein they will abide, with no desire to be removed from thence.
tr.22: Wherein they shall dwell (for aye): no change will they wish for from them.
tr.203: "Wherein they shall dwell (forever). No desire will they have for removal therefrom."

18.ar: قُل لَّوْ كَانَ ٱلْبَحْرُ مِدَادًا لِّكَلِمَـٰتِ رَبِّى لَنَفِدَ ٱلْبَحْرُ قَبْلَ أَن تَنفَدَ كَلِمَـٰتُ رَبِّى وَلَوْ جِئْنَا بِمِثْلِهِۦ مَدَدًا
18.en: Say, "If the sea were ink for [writing] the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it in [continual] supplement."
18.tl: qul law kāna l-baḥru midādan likalimāti rabbī lanafida l-baḥru qabla an tanfada kalimātu rabbī walaw ji'nā bimith'lihi madadan

tr.85: Say [Prophet], ‘If the whole ocean were ink for writing the words of my Lord, it would run dry before those words were exhausted’- even if We were to add another ocean to it.
tr.19: Say: Though the sea became ink for the Words of my Lord, verily the sea would be used up before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even though We brought the like thereof to help.
tr.22: Say: "If the ocean were ink (wherewith to write out) the words of my Lord, sooner would the ocean be exhausted than would the words of my Lord, even if we added another ocean like it, for its aid."
tr.203: Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم to mankind): "If the sea were ink for (writing) the Words of my Lord, surely, the sea would be exhausted before the Words of my Lord would be finished, even if We brought (another sea) like it for its aid."

18.ar: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَـٰهُكُمْ إِلَـٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ ۖ فَمَن كَانَ يَرْجُوا۟ لِقَآءَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلًا صَـٰلِحًا وَلَا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَحَدًۢا
18.en: Say, "I am only a man like you, to whom has been revealed that your god is one God. So whoever would hope for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone."
18.tl: qul innamā anā basharun mith'lukum yūḥā ilayya annamā ilāhukum ilāhun wāḥidun faman kāna yarjū liqāa rabbihi falyaʿmal ʿamalan ṣāliḥan walā yush'rik biʿibādati rabbihi aḥadan

tr.85: Say, ‘I am only a human being, like you, to whom it has been revealed that your God is One. Anyone who fears to meet his Lord should do good deeds and give no one a share in the worship due to his Lord.
tr.19: Say: I am only a mortal like you. My Lord inspireth in me that your Allah is only One Allah. And whoever hopeth for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work, and make none sharer of the worship due unto his Lord.
tr.22: Say: "I am but a man like yourselves, (but) the inspiration has come to me, that your Allah is one Allah: whoever expects to meet his Lord, let him work righteousness, and, in the worship of his Lord, admit no one as partner.
tr.203: Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم): "I am only a man like you. It has been revealed to me that your Ilâh (God) is One Ilâh (God - i.e. Allâh). So whoever hopes for the Meeting with his Lord, let him work righteousness and associate none as a partner in the worship of his Lord."

19.ar: كٓهيعٓصٓ
19.en: Kāf, Hā, Yā, ʿAyn, Ṣād.
19.tl: kaf-ha-ya-ain-sad

tr.85: Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad
tr.19: Kaf. Ha. Ya. A'in. Sad.
tr.22: Kaf. Ha. Ya. 'Ain. Sad.
tr.203: Kâf-Hâ-Yâ-‘Aîn-Sâd. [These letters are one of the miracles of the Qur’ân, and none but Allâh (Alone) knows their meanings].

19.ar: ذِكْرُ رَحْمَتِ رَبِّكَ عَبْدَهُۥ زَكَرِيَّآ
19.en: [This is] a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zechariah
19.tl: dhik'ru raḥmati rabbika ʿabdahu zakariyyā

tr.85: This is an account of your Lord’s grace towards His servant, Zachariah,
tr.19: A mention of the mercy of thy Lord unto His servant Zachariah.
tr.22: (This is) a recital of the Mercy of thy Lord to His servant Zakariya.
tr.203: (This is) a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His slave Zakariyyâ (Zachariah).

19.ar: إِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥ نِدَآءً خَفِيًّا
19.en: When he called to his Lord a private call [i.e., supplication].
19.tl: idh nādā rabbahu nidāan khafiyyan

tr.85: when he called to his Lord secretly, saying,
tr.19: When he cried unto his Lord a cry in secret,
tr.22: Behold! he cried to his Lord in secret,
tr.203: When he called out his Lord (Allâh) a call in secret.

19.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى وَهَنَ ٱلْعَظْمُ مِنِّى وَٱشْتَعَلَ ٱلرَّأْسُ شَيْبًا وَلَمْ أَكُنۢ بِدُعَآئِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا
19.en: He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has filled with white, and never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy [i.e., disappointed].
19.tl: qāla rabbi innī wahana l-ʿaẓmu minnī wa-ish'taʿala l-rasu shayban walam akun biduʿāika rabbi shaqiyyan

tr.85: ‘Lord, my bones have weakened and my hair is ashen grey, but never, Lord, have I ever prayed to You in vain:
tr.19: Saying: My Lord! Lo! the bones of me wax feeble and my head is shining with grey hair, and I have never been unblest in prayer to Thee, my Lord.
tr.22: Praying: "O my Lord! infirm indeed are my bones, and the hair of my head doth glisten with grey: but never am I unblest, O my Lord, in my prayer to Thee!
tr.203: He said: "My Lord! Indeed my bones have grown feeble, and grey hair has spread on my head, And I have never been unblest in my invocation to You, O my Lord!

19.ar: وَإِنِّى خِفْتُ ٱلْمَوَٰلِىَ مِن وَرَآءِى وَكَانَتِ ٱمْرَأَتِى عَاقِرًا فَهَبْ لِى مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِيًّا
19.en: And indeed, I fear the successors after me, and my wife has been barren, so give me from Yourself an heir
19.tl: wa-innī khif'tu l-mawāliya min warāī wakānati im'ra-atī ʿāqiran fahab lī min ladunka waliyyan

tr.85: I fear [what] my kinsmen [will do] when I am gone, for my wife is barren, so grant me a successor––a gift from You––
tr.19: Lo! I fear my kinsfolk after me, since my wife is barren. Oh, give me from Thy presence a successor
tr.22: "Now I fear (what) my relatives (and colleagues) (will do) after me: but my wife is barren: so give me an heir as from Thyself,-
tr.203: "And verily I fear my relatives after me, and my wife is barren. So give me from Yourself an heir.

19.ar: يَرِثُنِى وَيَرِثُ مِنْ ءَالِ يَعْقُوبَ ۖ وَٱجْعَلْهُ رَبِّ رَضِيًّا
19.en: Who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob. And make him, my Lord, pleasing [to You]."
19.tl: yarithunī wayarithu min āli yaʿqūba wa-ij'ʿalhu rabbi raḍiyyan

tr.85: to be my heir and the heir of the family of Jacob. Lord, make him well pleasing [to You].’
tr.19: Who shall inherit of me and inherit (also) of the house of Jacob. And make him, my Lord, acceptable (unto Thee).
tr.22: "(One that) will (truly) represent me, and represent the posterity of Jacob; and make him, O my Lord! one with whom Thou art well-pleased!"
tr.203: "Who shall inherit me, and inherit (also) the posterity of Ya‘qûb (Jacob) (inheritance of the religious knowledge and Prophethood, not of wealth.). And make him, my Lord, one with whom You are Well-Pleased!"

19.ar: يَـٰزَكَرِيَّآ إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَـٰمٍ ٱسْمُهُۥ يَحْيَىٰ لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا
19.en: [He was told], "O Zechariah, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John. We have not assigned to any before [this] name."
19.tl: yāzakariyyā innā nubashiruka bighulāmin us'muhu yaḥyā lam najʿal lahu min qablu samiyyan

tr.85: ‘Zachariah, We bring you good news of a son whose name will be John––We have chosen this name for no one before him.’
tr.19: (It was said unto him): O Zachariah! Lo! We bring thee tidings of a son whose name is John; we have given the same name to none before (him).
tr.22: (His prayer was answered): "O Zakariya! We give thee good news of a son: His name shall be Yahya: on none by that name have We conferred distinction before."
tr.203: (Allâh said) "O Zakariyyâ (Zachariah)! Verily, We give you the glad tidings of a son, whose name will be Yahyâ (John). We have given that name to none before (him)."

19.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَـٰمٌ وَكَانَتِ ٱمْرَأَتِى عَاقِرًا وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ ٱلْكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا
19.en: He said, "My Lord, how will I have a boy when my wife has been barren and I have reached extreme old age?"
19.tl: qāla rabbi annā yakūnu lī ghulāmun wakānati im'ra-atī ʿāqiran waqad balaghtu mina l-kibari ʿitiyyan

tr.85: He said, ‘Lord, how can I have a son when my wife is barren, and I am old and frail?’
tr.19: He said: My Lord! How can I have a son when my wife is barren and I have reached infirm old age?
tr.22: He said: "O my Lord! How shall I have a son, when my wife is barren and I have grown quite decrepit from old age?"
tr.203: He said: "My Lord! How can I have a son, when my wife is barren, and I have reached the extreme old age."

19.ar: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَىَّ هَيِّنٌ وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِن قَبْلُ وَلَمْ تَكُ شَيْـًٔا
19.en: [An angel] said, "Thus [it will be]; your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, for I created you before, while you were nothing.'"
19.tl: qāla kadhālika qāla rabbuka huwa ʿalayya hayyinun waqad khalaqtuka min qablu walam taku shayan

tr.85: He said, ‘This is what your Lord has said: “It is easy for Me: I created you, though you were nothing before.” ’
tr.19: He said: So (it will be). Thy Lord saith: It is easy for Me, even as I created thee before, when thou wast naught.
tr.22: He said: "So (it will be) thy Lord saith, 'that is easy for Me: I did indeed create thee before, when thou hadst been nothing!'"
tr.203: He said: "So (it will be). Your Lord says: It is easy for Me. Certainly I have created you before, when you had been nothing!"

19.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱجْعَل لِّىٓ ءَايَةً ۚ قَالَ ءَايَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ ٱلنَّاسَ ثَلَـٰثَ لَيَالٍ سَوِيًّا
19.en: [Zechariah] said, "My Lord, make for me a sign." He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, [being] sound."
19.tl: qāla rabbi ij'ʿal lī āyatan qāla āyatuka allā tukallima l-nāsa thalātha layālin sawiyyan

tr.85: He said, ‘Give me a sign, Lord.’ He said, ‘Your sign is that you will not [be able to] speak to anyone for three full [days and] nights.’
tr.19: He said: My Lord! Appoint for me some token. He said: Thy token is that thou, with no bodily defect, shalt not speak unto mankind three nights.
tr.22: (Zakariya) said: "O my Lord! give me a Sign." "Thy Sign," was the answer, "Shall be that thou shalt speak to no man for three nights, although thou art not dumb."
tr.203: [Zakariyyâ (Zachariah)] said: "My Lord! Appoint for me a sign." He said: "Your sign is that you shall not speak unto mankind for three nights, though having no bodily defect."

19.ar: فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلْمِحْرَابِ فَأَوْحَىٰٓ إِلَيْهِمْ أَن سَبِّحُوا۟ بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا
19.en: So he came out to his people from the prayer chamber and signaled to them to exalt [Allāh] in the morning and afternoon.
19.tl: fakharaja ʿalā qawmihi mina l-miḥ'rābi fa-awḥā ilayhim an sabbiḥū buk'ratan waʿashiyyan

tr.85: He went out of the sanctuary to his people and signalled to them to praise God morning and evening.
tr.19: Then he came forth unto his people from the sanctuary, and signified to them: Glorify your Lord at break of day and fall of night.
tr.22: So Zakariya came out to his people from him chamber: He told them by signs to celebrate Allah's praises in the morning and in the evening.
tr.203: Then he came out to his people from Al-Mihrâb (a praying place or a private room), and he told them by signs to glorify Allâh’s Praises in the morning and in the afternoon.

19.ar: يَـٰيَحْيَىٰ خُذِ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ بِقُوَّةٍ ۖ وَءَاتَيْنَـٰهُ ٱلْحُكْمَ صَبِيًّا
19.en: [Allāh said], "O John, take the Scripture [i.e., adhere to it] with determination." And We gave him judgement [while yet] a boy
19.tl: yāyaḥyā khudhi l-kitāba biquwwatin waātaynāhu l-ḥuk'ma ṣabiyyan

tr.85: [We said], ‘John, hold on to the Scripture firmly.’ While he was still a boy, We granted him wisdom,
tr.19: (And it was said unto his son): O John! Hold fast the Scripture. And we gave him wisdom when a child,
tr.22: (To his son came the command): "O Yahya! take hold of the Book with might": and We gave him Wisdom even as a youth,
tr.203: (It was said to his son): "O Yahyâ (John)! Hold fast the Scripture [the Taurât (Torah)]." And We gave him wisdom while yet a child.

19.ar: وَحَنَانًا مِّن لَّدُنَّا وَزَكَوٰةً ۖ وَكَانَ تَقِيًّا
19.en: And affection from Us and purity, and he was fearing of Allāh
19.tl: waḥanānan min ladunnā wazakatan wakāna taqiyyan

tr.85: tenderness from Us, and purity. He was devout,
tr.19: And compassion from Our presence, and purity; and he was devout,
tr.22: And piety (for all creatures) as from Us, and purity: He was devout,
tr.203: And (made him) sympathetic to men as a mercy (or a grant) from Us, and pure from sins [i.e. Yahyâ (John)] and he was righteous,

19.ar: وَبَرًّۢا بِوَٰلِدَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَكُن جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّا
19.en: And dutiful to his parents, and he was not a disobedient tyrant.
19.tl: wabarran biwālidayhi walam yakun jabbāran ʿaṣiyyan

tr.85: kind to his parents, not domineering or rebellious.
tr.19: And dutiful toward his parents. And he was not arrogant, rebellious.
tr.22: And kind to his parents, and he was not overbearing or rebellious.
tr.203: And dutiful towards his parents, and he was neither arrogant nor disobedient (to Allâh or to his parents).

19.ar: وَسَلَـٰمٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيًّا
19.en: And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he is raised alive.
19.tl: wasalāmun ʿalayhi yawma wulida wayawma yamūtu wayawma yub'ʿathu ḥayyan

tr.85: Peace was on him the day he was born, the day he died, and it will be on him the day he is raised to life again.
tr.19: Peace on him the day he was born, and the day he dieth and the day he shall be raised alive!
tr.22: So Peace on him the day he was born, the day that he dies, and the day that he will be raised up to life (again)!
tr.203: And Salâm (peace) be on him the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he will be raised up to life (again)!

19.ar: وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ مَرْيَمَ إِذِ ٱنتَبَذَتْ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا مَكَانًا شَرْقِيًّا
19.en: And mention, [O Muḥammad], in the Book [the story of] Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east.
19.tl: wa-udh'kur fī l-kitābi maryama idhi intabadhat min ahlihā makānan sharqiyyan

tr.85: Mention in the Quran the story of Mary. She withdrew from her family to a place to the east
tr.19: And make mention of Mary in the Scripture, when she had withdrawn from her people to a chamber looking East,
tr.22: Relate in the Book (the story of) Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place in the East.
tr.203: And mention in the Book (the Qur’ân, O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم the story of) Maryam (Mary), when she withdrew in seclusion from her family to a place facing east.

19.ar: فَٱتَّخَذَتْ مِن دُونِهِمْ حِجَابًا فَأَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَيْهَا رُوحَنَا فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا
19.en: And she took, in seclusion from them, a screen. Then We sent to her Our Angel [i.e., Gabriel], and he represented himself to her as a well-proportioned man.
19.tl: fa-ittakhadhat min dūnihim ḥijāban fa-arsalnā ilayhā rūḥanā fatamathala lahā basharan sawiyyan

tr.85: and secluded herself away; We sent Our Spirit to appear before her in the form of a perfected man.
tr.19: And had chosen seclusion from them. Then We sent unto her Our Spirit and it assumed for her the likeness of a perfect man.
tr.22: She placed a screen (to screen herself) from them; then We sent her our angel, and he appeared before her as a man in all respects.
tr.203: She placed a screen (to screen herself) from them; then We sent to her Our Ruh [angel Jibrîl (Gabriel)], and he appeared before her in the form of a man in all respects.

19.ar: قَالَتْ إِنِّىٓ أَعُوذُ بِٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ مِنكَ إِن كُنتَ تَقِيًّا
19.en: She said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, [so leave me], if you should be fearing of Allāh."
19.tl: qālat innī aʿūdhu bil-raḥmāni minka in kunta taqiyyan

tr.85: She said, ‘I seek the Lord of Mercy’s protection against you: if you have any fear of Him [do not approach]!’
tr.19: She said: Lo! I seek refuge in the Beneficent One from thee, if thou art Allah-fearing.
tr.22: She said: "I seek refuge from thee to (Allah) Most Gracious: (come not near) if thou dost fear Allah."
tr.203: She said: "Verily! I seek refuge with the Most Gracious (Allâh) from you, if you do fear Allâh."

19.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلَـٰمًا زَكِيًّا
19.en: He said, "I am only the messenger of your Lord to give you [news of] a pure boy [i.e., son]."
19.tl: qāla innamā anā rasūlu rabbiki li-ahaba laki ghulāman zakiyyan

tr.85: but he said, ‘I am but a Mes-senger from your Lord, [come] to announce to you the gift of a pure son.’
tr.19: He said: I am only a messenger of thy Lord, that I may bestow on thee a faultless son.
tr.22: He said: "Nay, I am only a messenger from thy Lord, (to announce) to thee the gift of a holy son.
tr.203: (The angel) said: "I am only a messenger from your Lord, (to announce) to you the gift of a righteous son."

19.ar: قَالَتْ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِى غُلَـٰمٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِى بَشَرٌ وَلَمْ أَكُ بَغِيًّا
19.en: She said, "How can I have a boy while no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?"
19.tl: qālat annā yakūnu lī ghulāmun walam yamsasnī basharun walam aku baghiyyan

tr.85: She said, ‘How can I have a son when no man has touched me? I have not been unchaste,’
tr.19: She said: How can I have a son when no mortal hath touched me, neither have I been unchaste?
tr.22: She said: "How shall I have a son, seeing that no man has touched me, and I am not unchaste?"
tr.203: She said: "How can I have a son, when no man has touched me, nor am I unchaste?"

19.ar: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ هُوَ عَلَىَّ هَيِّنٌ ۖ وَلِنَجْعَلَهُۥٓ ءَايَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَرَحْمَةً مِّنَّا ۚ وَكَانَ أَمْرًا مَّقْضِيًّا
19.en: He said, "Thus [it will be]; your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign to the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter [already] decreed.'"
19.tl: qāla kadhāliki qāla rabbuki huwa ʿalayya hayyinun walinajʿalahu āyatan lilnnāsi waraḥmatan minnā wakāna amran maqḍiyyan

tr.85: and he said, ‘This is what your Lord said: “It is easy for Me- We shall make him a sign to all people, a blessing from Us.”’
tr.19: He said: So (it will be). Thy Lord saith: It is easy for Me. And (it will be) that We may make of him a revelation for mankind and a mercy from Us, and it is a thing ordained.
tr.22: He said: "So (it will be): Thy Lord saith, 'that is easy for Me: and (We wish) to appoint him as a Sign unto men and a Mercy from Us': It is a matter (so) decreed."
tr.203: He said: "So (it will be), your Lord said: ‘That is easy for Me (Allâh): And (We wish) to appoint him as a sign to mankind and a mercy from Us (Allâh), and it is a matter (already) decreed, (by Allâh).’ "

19.ar: ۞ فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَٱنتَبَذَتْ بِهِۦ مَكَانًا قَصِيًّا
19.en: So she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a remote place.
19.tl: faḥamalathu fa-intabadhat bihi makānan qaṣiyyan

tr.85: And so it was ordained: she conceived him. She withdrew to a distant place
tr.19: And she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a far place.
tr.22: So she conceived him, and she retired with him to a remote place.
tr.203: So she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a far place (i.e. Bethlehem valley about 4-6 miles from Jerusalem).

19.ar: فَأَجَآءَهَا ٱلْمَخَاضُ إِلَىٰ جِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ قَالَتْ يَـٰلَيْتَنِى مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَـٰذَا وَكُنتُ نَسْيًا مَّنسِيًّا
19.en: And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, "Oh, I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten."
19.tl: fa-ajāahā l-makhāḍu ilā jidh'ʿi l-nakhlati qālat yālaytanī mittu qabla hādhā wakuntu nasyan mansiyyan

tr.85: and, when the pains of childbirth drove her to [cling to] the trunk of a palm tree, she exclaimed, ‘I wish I had been dead and forgotten long before all this!’
tr.19: And the pangs of childbirth drove her unto the trunk of the palm-tree. She said: Oh, would that I had died ere this and had become a thing of naught, forgotten!
tr.22: And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm-tree: She cried (in her anguish): "Ah! would that I had died before this! would that I had been a thing forgotten and out of sight!"
tr.203: And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a date-palm. She said: "Would that I had died before this, and had been forgotten and out of sight!"

19.ar: فَنَادَىٰهَا مِن تَحْتِهَآ أَلَّا تَحْزَنِى قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا
19.en: But he called her from below her, "Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream.
19.tl: fanādāhā min taḥtihā allā taḥzanī qad jaʿala rabbuki taḥtaki sariyyan

tr.85: but a voice cried to her from below, ‘Do not worry: your Lord has provided a stream at your feet
tr.19: Then (one) cried unto her from below her, saying: Grieve not! Thy Lord hath placed a rivulet beneath thee,
tr.22: But (a voice) cried to her from beneath the (palm-tree): "Grieve not! for thy Lord hath provided a rivulet beneath thee;
tr.203: Then [the babe ‘Îsâ (Jesus) or Jibrîl (Gabriel)] cried unto her from below her, saying: "Grieve not: your Lord has provided a water stream under you.

19.ar: وَهُزِّىٓ إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ تُسَـٰقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا
19.en: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates.
19.tl: wahuzzī ilayki bijidh'ʿi l-nakhlati tusāqiṭ ʿalayki ruṭaban janiyyan

tr.85: and, if you shake the trunk of the palm tree towards you, it will deliver fresh ripe dates for you,
tr.19: And shake the trunk of the palm-tree toward thee, thou wilt cause ripe dates to fall upon thee.
tr.22: "And shake towards thyself the trunk of the palm-tree: It will let fall fresh ripe dates upon thee.
tr.203: "And shake the trunk of date-palm towards you, it will let fall fresh ripe-dates upon you."

19.ar: فَكُلِى وَٱشْرَبِى وَقَرِّى عَيْنًا ۖ فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا فَقُولِىٓ إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ صَوْمًا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِنسِيًّا
19.en: So eat and drink and be contented. And if you see from among humanity anyone, say, 'Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful abstention, so I will not speak today to [any] man.'"
19.tl: fakulī wa-ish'rabī waqarrī ʿaynan fa-immā tarayinna mina l-bashari aḥadan faqūlī innī nadhartu lilrraḥmāni ṣawman falan ukallima l-yawma insiyyan

tr.85: so eat, drink, be glad, and say to anyone you may see: “I have vowed to the Lord of Mercy to abstain from conversation, and I will not talk to anyone today.”’
tr.19: So eat and drink and be consoled. And if thou meetest any mortal, say: Lo! I have vowed a fast unto the Beneficent, and may not speak this day to any mortal.
tr.22: "So eat and drink and cool (thine) eye. And if thou dost see any man, say, 'I have vowed a fast to (Allah) Most Gracious, and this day will I enter into not talk with any human being'"
tr.203: "So eat and drink and be glad. And if you see any human being, say: ‘Verily! I have vowed a fast unto the Most Gracious (Allâh) so I shall not speak to any human being this day.’"

19.ar: فَأَتَتْ بِهِۦ قَوْمَهَا تَحْمِلُهُۥ ۖ قَالُوا۟ يَـٰمَرْيَمُ لَقَدْ جِئْتِ شَيْـًٔا فَرِيًّا
19.en: Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, "O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented.
19.tl: fa-atat bihi qawmahā taḥmiluhu qālū yāmaryamu laqad ji'ti shayan fariyyan

tr.85: She went back to her people carrying the child, and they said, ‘Mary! You have done something terrible!
tr.19: Then she brought him to her own folk, carrying him. They said: O Mary! Thou hast come with an amazing thing.
tr.22: At length she brought the (babe) to her people, carrying him (in her arms). They said: "O Mary! truly an amazing thing hast thou brought!
tr.203: Then she brought him (the baby) to her people, carrying him. They said: "O Mary! Indeed you have brought a thing Fariyy (a mighty thing). [Tafsir Al-Tabari]

19.ar: يَـٰٓأُخْتَ هَـٰرُونَ مَا كَانَ أَبُوكِ ٱمْرَأَ سَوْءٍ وَمَا كَانَتْ أُمُّكِ بَغِيًّا
19.en: O sister [i.e., descendant] of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste."
19.tl: yāukh'ta hārūna mā kāna abūki im'ra-a sawin wamā kānat ummuki baghiyyan

tr.85: Sister of Aaron! Your father was not an evil man; your mother was not unchaste!’
tr.19: O sister of Aaron! Thy father was not a wicked man nor was thy mother a harlot.
tr.22: "O sister of Aaron! Thy father was not a man of evil, nor thy mother a woman unchaste!"
tr.203: "O sister (i.e. the like) of Hârûn (Aaron)! Your father was not a man who used to commit adultery, nor your mother was an unchaste woman."

19.ar: فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ ۖ قَالُوا۟ كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَن كَانَ فِى ٱلْمَهْدِ صَبِيًّا
19.en: So she pointed to him. They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle a child?"
19.tl: fa-ashārat ilayhi qālū kayfa nukallimu man kāna fī l-mahdi ṣabiyyan

tr.85: She pointed at him. They said, ‘How can we converse with an infant?’
tr.19: Then she pointed to him. They said: How can we talk to one who is in the cradle, a young boy?
tr.22: But she pointed to the babe. They said: "How can we talk to one who is a child in the cradle?"
tr.203: Then she pointed to him. They said: "How can we talk to one who is a child in the cradle?"

19.ar: قَالَ إِنِّى عَبْدُ ٱللَّهِ ءَاتَىٰنِىَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ وَجَعَلَنِى نَبِيًّا
19.en: [Jesus] said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allāh. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.
19.tl: qāla innī ʿabdu l-lahi ātāniya l-kitāba wajaʿalanī nabiyyan

tr.85: [But] he said: ‘I am a servant of God. He has granted me the Scripture; made me a prophet;
tr.19: He spake: Lo! I am the slave of Allah. He hath given me the Scripture and hath appointed me a Prophet,
tr.22: He said: "I am indeed a servant of Allah: He hath given me revelation and made me a prophet;
tr.203: "He [‘Îsâ (Jesus)] said: "Verily I am a slave of Allâh, He has given me the Scripture and made me a Prophet;"

19.ar: وَجَعَلَنِى مُبَارَكًا أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُ وَأَوْصَـٰنِى بِٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَٱلزَّكَوٰةِ مَا دُمْتُ حَيًّا
19.en: And He has made me blessed wherever I am and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakāh as long as I remain alive
19.tl: wajaʿalanī mubārakan ayna mā kuntu wa-awṣānī bil-ṣalati wal-zakati mā dum'tu ḥayyan

tr.85: made me blessed wherever I may be. He commanded me to pray, to give alms as long as I live,
tr.19: And hath made me blessed wheresoever I may be, and hath enjoined upon me prayer and almsgiving so long as I remain alive,
tr.22: "And He hath made me blessed wheresoever I be, and hath enjoined on me Prayer and Charity as long as I live;
tr.203: "And He has made me blessed wheresoever I be, and has enjoined on me Salât (prayer), and Zakât, as long as I live."

19.ar: وَبَرًّۢا بِوَٰلِدَتِى وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْنِى جَبَّارًا شَقِيًّا
19.en: And [made me] dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a wretched tyrant.
19.tl: wabarran biwālidatī walam yajʿalnī jabbāran shaqiyyan

tr.85: to cherish my mother. He did not make me domineering or graceless.
tr.19: And (hath made me) dutiful toward her who bore me, and hath not made me arrogant, unblest.
tr.22: "(He) hath made me kind to my mother, and not overbearing or miserable;
tr.203: "And dutiful to my mother, and made me not arrogant, unblest.

19.ar: وَٱلسَّلَـٰمُ عَلَىَّ يَوْمَ وُلِدتُّ وَيَوْمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ أُبْعَثُ حَيًّا
19.en: And peace is on me the day I was born and the day I will die and the day I am raised alive."
19.tl: wal-salāmu ʿalayya yawma wulidttu wayawma amūtu wayawma ub'ʿathu ḥayyan

tr.85: Peace was on me the day I was born, and will be on me the day I die and the day I am raised to life again.’
