25.en: So they will deny you, [disbelievers], in what you say, and you cannot avert [punishment] or [find] help. And whoever commits injustice among you - We will make him taste a great punishment.
25.tl: faqad kadhabūkum bimā taqūlūna famā tastaṭīʿūna ṣarfan walā naṣran waman yaẓlim minkum nudhiq'hu ʿadhāban kabīran

tr.85: [God will say], ‘Now your gods have denounced what you say as lies: you cannot avoid the punishment; you will not get any help.’ If any of you commits such evil, We shall make him taste agonizing torment.
tr.19: Thus they will give you the lie regarding what ye say, then ye can neither avert (the doom) nor obtain help. And whoso among you doeth wrong, We shall make him taste great torment.
tr.22: (Allah will say): "Now have they proved you liars in what ye say: so ye cannot avert (your penalty) nor (get) help." And whoever among you does wrong, him shall We cause to taste of a grievous Penalty.
tr.203: Thus they (false gods - all deities other than Allâh) will belie you (polytheists) regarding what you say (that they are gods besides Allâh): then you can neither avert (the punishment), nor get help. And whoever among you does wrong (i.e. sets up rivals to Allâh), We shall make him taste a great torment.

25.ar: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّآ إِنَّهُمْ لَيَأْكُلُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ وَيَمْشُونَ فِى ٱلْأَسْوَاقِ ۗ وَجَعَلْنَا بَعْضَكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ فِتْنَةً أَتَصْبِرُونَ ۗ وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ بَصِيرًا
25.en: And We did not send before you, [O Muḥammad], any of the messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. And We have made some of you [people] as trial for others - will you have patience? And ever is your Lord, Seeing.
25.tl: wamā arsalnā qablaka mina l-mur'salīna illā innahum layakulūna l-ṭaʿāma wayamshūna fī l-aswāqi wajaʿalnā baʿḍakum libaʿḍin fit'natan ataṣbirūna wakāna rabbuka baṣīran

tr.85: No messenger have We sent before you [Muhammad] who did not eat food and walk about in the marketplace. But We have made some of you a means of testing others- will you stand fast? Your Lord is always watching.
tr.19: We never sent before thee any messengers but lo! they verily ate food and walked in the markets. And We have appointed some of you a test for others: Will ye be steadfast? And thy Lord is ever Seer.
tr.22: And the messengers whom We sent before thee were all (men) who ate food and walked through the streets: We have made some of you as a trial for others: will ye have patience? for Allah is One Who sees (all things).
tr.203: And We never sent before you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) any of the Messengers but verily, they ate food and walked in the markets. And We have made some of you as a trial for others: will you have patience? And your Lord is Ever All-Seer (of everything).

25.ar: ۞ وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ لِقَآءَنَا لَوْلَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيْنَا ٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةُ أَوْ نَرَىٰ رَبَّنَا ۗ لَقَدِ ٱسْتَكْبَرُوا۟ فِىٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَعَتَوْ عُتُوًّا كَبِيرًا
25.en: And those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, "Why were not angels sent down to us, or [why] do we [not] see our Lord?" They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and [become] insolent with great insolence.
25.tl: waqāla alladhīna lā yarjūna liqāanā lawlā unzila ʿalaynā l-malāikatu aw narā rabbanā laqadi is'takbarū fī anfusihim waʿataw ʿutuwwan kabīran

tr.85: Those who do not fear to meet Us say, ‘Why are the angels not sent down to us?’ or ‘Why can we not see our Lord?’ They are too proud of themselves and too insolent.
tr.19: And those who look not for a meeting with Us say: Why are angels not sent down unto us and (Why) do we not see our Lord! Assuredly they think too highly of themselves and are scornful with great pride.
tr.22: Such as fear not the meeting with Us (for Judgment) say: "Why are not the angels sent down to us, or (why) do we not see our Lord?" Indeed they have an arrogant conceit of themselves, and mighty is the insolence of their impiety!
tr.203: And those who expect not a Meeting with Us (i.e. those who deny the Day of Resurrection and the life of the Hereafter) said: "Why are not the angels sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" Indeed they think too highly of themselves, and are scornful with great pride.

25.ar: يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ ٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةَ لَا بُشْرَىٰ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْرًا مَّحْجُورًا
25.en: The day they see the angels - no good tidings will there be that day for the criminals, and [the angels] will say, "Prevented and inaccessible."
25.tl: yawma yarawna l-malāikata lā bush'rā yawma-idhin lil'muj'rimīna wayaqūlūna ḥij'ran maḥjūran

tr.85: There will be no good news for the guilty on the Day they see the angels. The angels will say, ‘You cannot cross the forbidden barrier,’
tr.19: On the day when they behold the angels, on that day there will be no good tidings for the guilty; and they will cry: A forbidding ban!
tr.22: The Day they see the angels,- no joy will there be to the sinners that Day: The (angels) will say: "There is a barrier forbidden (to you) altogether!"
tr.203: On the Day they will see the angels - no glad tidings will there be for the Mujrimûn (criminals, disbelievers, polytheists, sinners) that day. And they (angels) will say: "All kinds of glad tidings are forbidden to you," [none will be allowed to enter Paradise except the one who said: Lâ ilâha illallâh, "(none has the right to be worshipped but Allâh) and acted practically on its legal orders and obligations. See the footnote of V.2:193)].

25.ar: وَقَدِمْنَآ إِلَىٰ مَا عَمِلُوا۟ مِنْ عَمَلٍ فَجَعَلْنَـٰهُ هَبَآءً مَّنثُورًا
25.en: And We will approach [i.e., regard] what they have done of deeds and make them as dust dispersed.
25.tl: waqadim'nā ilā mā ʿamilū min ʿamalin fajaʿalnāhu habāan manthūran

tr.85: and We shall turn to the deeds they have done and scatter them like dust.
tr.19: And We shall turn unto the work they did and make it scattered motes.
tr.22: And We shall turn to whatever deeds they did (in this life), and We shall make such deeds as floating dust scattered about.
tr.203: And We shall turn to whatever deeds they (disbelievers, polytheists, sinners) did, and We shall make such deeds as scattered floating particles of dust.

25.ar: أَصْحَـٰبُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرًّا وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلًا
25.en: The companions of Paradise, that Day, are [in] a better settlement and better resting place.
25.tl: aṣḥābu l-janati yawma-idhin khayrun mus'taqarran wa-aḥsanu maqīlan

tr.85: But the companions in the Garden will have a better home on that Day, and a fairer place to rest.
tr.19: Those who have earned the Garden on that day will be better in their home and happier in their place of noonday rest;
tr.22: The Companions of the Garden will be well, that Day, in their abode, and have the fairest of places for repose.
tr.203: The dwellers of Paradise (i.e. those who deserved it through their Islamic Monotheistic Faith and their deeds of righteousness) will, on that Day, have the best abode, and have the fairest of places for repose.

25.ar: وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِٱلْغَمَـٰمِ وَنُزِّلَ ٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةُ تَنزِيلًا
25.en: And [mention] the Day when the heaven will split open with [emerging] clouds, and the angels will be sent down in successive descent.
25.tl: wayawma tashaqqaqu l-samāu bil-ghamāmi wanuzzila l-malāikatu tanzīlan

tr.85: On the Day when the sky and its clouds are split apart and the angels sent down in streams,
tr.19: A day when the heaven with the clouds will be rent asunder and the angels will be sent down, a grand descent.
tr.22: The Day the heaven shall be rent asunder with clouds, and angels shall be sent down, descending (in ranks),-
tr.203: And (remember) the Day when the heaven shall be rent asunder with clouds, and the angels will be sent down, with a grand descending.

25.ar: ٱلْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْحَقُّ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ۚ وَكَانَ يَوْمًا عَلَى ٱلْكَـٰفِرِينَ عَسِيرًا
25.en: True sovereignty, that Day, is for the Most Merciful. And it will be upon the disbelievers a difficult Day.
25.tl: al-mul'ku yawma-idhin l-ḥaqu lilrraḥmāni wakāna yawman ʿalā l-kāfirīna ʿasīran

tr.85: on that Day, true authority belongs to the Lord of Mercy. It will be a grievous Day for the disbelievers.
tr.19: The Sovereignty on that day will be the True (Sovereignty) belonging to the Beneficent One, and it will be a hard day for disbelievers.
tr.22: That Day, the dominion as of right and truth, shall be (wholly) for (Allah) Most Merciful: it will be a Day of dire difficulty for the misbelievers.
tr.203: The sovereignty on that Day will be the true (sovereignty), belonging to the Most Gracious (Allâh), and it will be a hard Day for the disbelievers (those who disbelieve in the Oneness of Allâh - Islâmic Monotheism).

25.ar: وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ ٱلظَّالِمُ عَلَىٰ يَدَيْهِ يَقُولُ يَـٰلَيْتَنِى ٱتَّخَذْتُ مَعَ ٱلرَّسُولِ سَبِيلًا
25.en: And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands [in regret] he will say, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way.
25.tl: wayawma yaʿaḍḍu l-ẓālimu ʿalā yadayhi yaqūlu yālaytanī ittakhadhtu maʿa l-rasūli sabīlan

tr.85: On that Day the evildoer will bite his own hand and say, ‘If only I had taken the same path as the Messenger.
tr.19: On the day when the wrong-doer gnaweth his hands, he will say: Ah, would that I had chosen a way together with the messenger (of Allah)!
tr.22: The Day that the wrong-doer will bite at his hands, he will say, "Oh! would that I had taken a (straight) path with the Messenger!
tr.203: And (remember) the Day when the Zâlim (wrong-doer, oppressor, polytheist) will bite at his hands, he will say: "Oh! Would that I had taken a path with the Messenger (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم).

25.ar: يَـٰوَيْلَتَىٰ لَيْتَنِى لَمْ أَتَّخِذْ فُلَانًا خَلِيلًا
25.en: Oh, woe to me! I wish I had not taken that one as a friend.
25.tl: yāwaylatā laytanī lam attakhidh fulānan khalīlan

tr.85: Woe is me! If only I had not taken so and so as a friend-
tr.19: Alas for me! Ah, would that I had never taken such an one for friend!
tr.22: "Ah! woe is me! Would that I had never taken such a one for a friend!
tr.203: "Ah! Woe to me! Would that I had never taken so-and-so as a Khalîl (an intimate friend)!

25.ar: لَّقَدْ أَضَلَّنِى عَنِ ٱلذِّكْرِ بَعْدَ إِذْ جَآءَنِى ۗ وَكَانَ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنُ لِلْإِنسَـٰنِ خَذُولًا
25.en: He led me away from the remembrance after it had come to me. And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter."
25.tl: laqad aḍallanī ʿani l-dhik'ri baʿda idh jāanī wakāna l-shayṭānu lil'insāni khadhūlan

tr.85: he led me away from the Revelation after it reached me. Satan has always betrayed mankind.’
tr.19: He verily led me astray from the Reminder after it had reached me. Satan was ever man's deserter in the hour of need.
tr.22: "He did lead me astray from the Message (of Allah) after it had come to me! Ah! the Evil One is but a traitor to man!"
tr.203: "He indeed led me astray from the Reminder (this Qur’ân) after it had come to me. And Shaitân (Satan) is to man ever a deserter in the hour of need." [Tafsir Al-Qurtubi]

25.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلرَّسُولُ يَـٰرَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِى ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ مَهْجُورًا
25.en: And the Messenger has said, "O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur’ān as [a thing] abandoned."
25.tl: waqāla l-rasūlu yārabbi inna qawmī ittakhadhū hādhā l-qur'āna mahjūran

tr.85: The Messenger has said, ‘Lord, my people treat this Quran as something to be shunned,’
tr.19: And the messenger saith: O my Lord! Lo! mine own folk make this Qur'an of no account.
tr.22: Then the Messenger will say: "O my Lord! Truly my people took this Qur'an for just foolish nonsense."
tr.203: And the Messenger (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) will say: "O my Lord! Verily, my people deserted this Qur’ân (neither listened to it, nor acted on its laws and teachings).

25.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِىٍّ عَدُوًّا مِّنَ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِرَبِّكَ هَادِيًا وَنَصِيرًا
25.en: And thus have We made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. But sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper.
25.tl: wakadhālika jaʿalnā likulli nabiyyin ʿaduwwan mina l-muj'rimīna wakafā birabbika hādiyan wanaṣīran

tr.85: but We have always appointed adversaries from the wicked, for every prophet: Your Lord is sufficient guide and helper.
tr.19: Even so have We appointed unto every prophet an opponent from among the guilty; but Allah sufficeth for a Guide and Helper.
tr.22: Thus have We made for every prophet an enemy among the sinners: but enough is thy Lord to guide and to help.
tr.203: Thus have We made for every Prophet an enemy among the Mujrimûn (disbelievers, polytheists, criminals). But Sufficient is your Lord as a Guide and Helper.

25.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةً وَٰحِدَةً ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِۦ فُؤَادَكَ ۖ وَرَتَّلْنَـٰهُ تَرْتِيلًا
25.en: And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur’ān not revealed to him all at once?" Thus [it is] that We may strengthen thereby your heart. And We have spaced it distinctly.
25.tl: waqāla alladhīna kafarū lawlā nuzzila ʿalayhi l-qur'ānu jum'latan wāḥidatan kadhālika linuthabbita bihi fuādaka warattalnāhu tartīlan

tr.85: The disbelievers also say, ‘Why was the Quran not sent down to him all at once?’ We sent it in this way to strengthen your heart [Prophet]; We gave it to you in gradual revelation.
tr.19: And those who disbelieve say: Why is the Qur'an not revealed unto him all at once? (It is revealed) thus that We may strengthen thy heart therewith; and We have arranged it in right order.
tr.22: Those who reject Faith say: "Why is not the Qur'an revealed to him all at once? Thus (is it revealed), that We may strengthen thy heart thereby, and We have rehearsed it to thee in slow, well-arranged stages, gradually.
tr.203: And those who disbelieve say: "Why is not the Qur’ân revealed to him all at once?" Thus (it is sent down in parts), that We may strengthen your heart thereby. And We have revealed it to you gradually, in stages. (It was revealed to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم in 23 years.).

25.ar: وَلَا يَأْتُونَكَ بِمَثَلٍ إِلَّا جِئْنَـٰكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَأَحْسَنَ تَفْسِيرًا
25.en: And they do not come to you with an example [i.e., argument] except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation.
25.tl: walā yatūnaka bimathalin illā ji'nāka bil-ḥaqi wa-aḥsana tafsīran

tr.85: They cannot put any argument to you without Our bringing you the truth and the best explanation.
tr.19: And they bring thee no similitude but We bring thee the Truth (as against it), and better (than their similitude) as argument.
tr.22: And no question do they bring to thee but We reveal to thee the truth and the best explanation (thereof).
tr.203: And no example or similitude do they bring (to oppose or to find fault in you or in this Qur’ân), but We reveal to you the truth (against that similitude or example), and the better explanation thereof.

25.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ شَرٌّ مَّكَانًا وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا
25.en: The ones who are gathered on their faces to Hell - those are the worst in position and farthest astray in [their] way.
25.tl: alladhīna yuḥ'sharūna ʿalā wujūhihim ilā jahannama ulāika sharrun makānan wa-aḍallu sabīlan

tr.85: It is those driven [falling], on their faces,to Hell who will be in the worst place- they are the furthest from the right path.
tr.19: Those who will be gathered on their faces unto hell: such are worse in plight and further from the right road.
tr.22: Those who will be gathered to Hell (prone) on their faces,- they will be in an evil plight, and, as to Path, most astray.
tr.203: Those who will be gathered to Hell (prone) on their faces, such will be in an evil state, and most astray from the (Straight) Path.

25.ar: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ وَجَعَلْنَا مَعَهُۥٓ أَخَاهُ هَـٰرُونَ وَزِيرًا
25.en: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture and appointed with him his brother Aaron as an assistant.
25.tl: walaqad ātaynā mūsā l-kitāba wajaʿalnā maʿahu akhāhu hārūna wazīran

tr.85: We gave Moses the Book and appointed his brother Aaron to help him.
tr.19: We verily gave Moses the Scripture and placed with him his brother Aaron as henchman.
tr.22: (Before this,) We sent Moses The Book, and appointed his brother Aaron with him as minister;
tr.203: And indeed We gave Mûsâ (Moses) the Scripture [the Taurât (Torah)], and placed his brother Hârûn (Aaron) with him as a helper;

25.ar: فَقُلْنَا ٱذْهَبَآ إِلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا فَدَمَّرْنَـٰهُمْ تَدْمِيرًا
25.en: And We said, "Go both of you to the people who have denied Our signs." Then We destroyed them with [complete] destruction.
25.tl: faqul'nā idh'habā ilā l-qawmi alladhīna kadhabū biāyātinā fadammarnāhum tadmīran

tr.85: We said, ‘Go, both of you, to the people who have rejected Our signs.’ Later We destroyed those people utterly.
tr.19: Then We said: Go together unto the folk who have denied Our revelations. Then We destroyed them, a complete destruction.
tr.22: And We command: "Go ye both, to the people who have rejected our Signs:" And those (people) We destroyed with utter destruction.
tr.203: And We said: "Go you both to the people who have denied Our Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.)." Then We destroyed them with utter destruction.

25.ar: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَّمَّا كَذَّبُوا۟ ٱلرُّسُلَ أَغْرَقْنَـٰهُمْ وَجَعَلْنَـٰهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ ءَايَةً ۖ وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلظَّـٰلِمِينَ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا
25.en: And the people of Noah - when they denied the messengers, We drowned them, and We made them for mankind a sign. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment.
25.tl: waqawma nūḥin lammā kadhabū l-rusula aghraqnāhum wajaʿalnāhum lilnnāsi āyatan wa-aʿtadnā lilẓẓālimīna ʿadhāban alīman

tr.85: The people of Noah, too: when they rejected their messengers, We drowned them and made them an example to all people. We have prepared a painful torment for the evildoers,
tr.19: And Noah's folk, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them and made of them a portent for mankind. We have prepared a painful doom for evil-doers.
tr.22: And the people of Noah,- when they rejected the messengers, We drowned them, and We made them as a Sign for mankind; and We have prepared for (all) wrong-doers a grievous Penalty;-
tr.203: And Nûh’s (Noah) people, when they denied the Messengers, We drowned them, and We made them as a sign for mankind. And We have prepared a painful torment for the Zâlimûn (polytheists and wrong-doers).

25.ar: وَعَادًا وَثَمُودَا۟ وَأَصْحَـٰبَ ٱلرَّسِّ وَقُرُونًۢا بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ كَثِيرًا
25.en: And [We destroyed] ʿAad and Thamūd and the companions of the well and many generations between them.
25.tl: waʿādan wathamūdā wa-aṣḥāba l-rasi waqurūnan bayna dhālika kathīran

tr.85: as We did for the people of Ad, Thamud, and al-Rass, and many generations in between.
tr.19: And (the tribes of) A'ad and Thamud, and the dwellers in Ar-Rass, and many generations in between.
tr.22: As also 'Ad and Thamud, and the Companions of the Rass, and many a generation between them.
tr.203: And (also) ‘Âd and Thamûd, and the Dwellers of Ar-Rass, and many generations in between.

25.ar: وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنَا لَهُ ٱلْأَمْثَـٰلَ ۖ وَكُلًّا تَبَّرْنَا تَتْبِيرًا
25.en: And for each We presented examples [as warnings], and each We destroyed with [total] destruction.
25.tl: wakullan ḍarabnā lahu l-amthāla wakullan tabbarnā tatbīran

tr.85: To each of them We gave warnings, and each of them We destroyed completely.
tr.19: Each (of them) We warned by examples, and each (of them) We brought to utter ruin.
tr.22: To each one We set forth Parables and examples; and each one We broke to utter annihilation (for their sins).
tr.203: And for each (of them) We put forward examples (as proofs and lessons), and each (of them) We brought to utter ruin (because of their disbelief and evil deeds).

25.ar: وَلَقَدْ أَتَوْا۟ عَلَى ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلَّتِىٓ أُمْطِرَتْ مَطَرَ ٱلسَّوْءِ ۚ أَفَلَمْ يَكُونُوا۟ يَرَوْنَهَا ۚ بَلْ كَانُوا۟ لَا يَرْجُونَ نُشُورًا
25.en: And they have already come upon the town which was showered with a rain of evil [i.e., stones]. So have they not seen it? But they are not expecting resurrection.
25.tl: walaqad ataw ʿalā l-qaryati allatī um'ṭirat maṭara l-sawi afalam yakūnū yarawnahā bal kānū lā yarjūna nushūran

tr.85: These disbelievers must have passed by the town that was destroyed by the terrible rain––did they not see it? Yet they do not expect to be raised from the dead.
tr.19: And indeed they have passed by the township whereon was rained the fatal rain. Can it be that they have not seen it? Nay, but they hope for no resurrection.
tr.22: And the (Unbelievers) must indeed have passed by the town on which was rained a shower of evil: did they not then see it (with their own eyes)? But they fear not the Resurrection.
tr.203: And indeed they have passed by the town [of Prophet Lût (Lot)] on which was rained the evil rain. Did they (disbelievers) not then see it (with their own eyes)? Nay! But they used not to expect any resurrection.

25.ar: وَإِذَا رَأَوْكَ إِن يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِى بَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ رَسُولًا
25.en: And when they see you, [O Muḥammad], they take you not except in ridicule, [saying], "Is this the one whom Allāh has sent as a messenger?
25.tl: wa-idhā ra-awka in yattakhidhūnaka illā huzuwan ahādhā alladhī baʿatha l-lahu rasūlan

tr.85: Whenever they see you [Prophet] they ridicule you: ‘Is this the one God has sent as a messenger?
tr.19: And when they see thee (O Muhammad) they treat thee only as a jest (saying): Is this he whom Allah sendeth as a messenger?
tr.22: When they see thee, they treat thee no otherwise than in mockery: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"
tr.203: And when they see you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم), they treat you only in mockery (saying): "Is this the one whom Allâh has sent as a Messenger?

25.ar: إِن كَادَ لَيُضِلُّنَا عَنْ ءَالِهَتِنَا لَوْلَآ أَن صَبَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا ۚ وَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ حِينَ يَرَوْنَ ٱلْعَذَابَ مَنْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا
25.en: He almost would have misled us from our gods had we not been steadfast in [worship of] them." But they are going to know, when they see the punishment, who is farthest astray in [his] way.
25.tl: in kāda layuḍillunā ʿan ālihatinā lawlā an ṣabarnā ʿalayhā wasawfa yaʿlamūna ḥīna yarawna l-ʿadhāba man aḍallu sabīlan

tr.85: He might almost have led us astray from our gods if we had not stood so firmly by them.’ When they see the punishment, they will know who is furthest from the path.
tr.19: He would have led us far away from our gods if we had not been staunch to them. They will know, when they behold the doom, who is more astray as to the road.
tr.22: "He indeed would well-nigh have misled us from our gods, had it not been that we were constant to them!" - Soon will they know, when they see the Penalty, who it is that is most misled in Path!
tr.203: "He would have nearly misled us from our âlihah (gods), had it not been that we were patient and constant in their worship!" And they will know when they see the torment, who it is that is most astray from the (Right) Path!

25.ar: أَرَءَيْتَ مَنِ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُۥ هَوَىٰهُ أَفَأَنتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَكِيلًا
25.en: Have you seen the one who takes as his god his own desire? Then would you be responsible for him?
25.tl: ara-ayta mani ittakhadha ilāhahu hawāhu afa-anta takūnu ʿalayhi wakīlan

tr.85: Think [Prophet] of the man who has taken his own passion as a god: are you to be his guardian?
tr.19: Hast thou seen him who chooseth for his god his own lust? Wouldst thou then be guardian over him?
tr.22: Seest thou such a one as taketh for his god his own passion (or impulse)? Couldst thou be a disposer of affairs for him?
tr.203: Have you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) seen him who has taken as his ilâh (god) his own vain desire? Would you then be a Wakîl (a disposer of his affairs or a watcher) over him?

25.ar: أَمْ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ أَوْ يَعْقِلُونَ ۚ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا كَٱلْأَنْعَـٰمِ ۖ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا
25.en: Or do you think that most of them hear or reason? They are not except like livestock. Rather, they are [even] more astray in [their] way.
25.tl: am taḥsabu anna aktharahum yasmaʿūna aw yaʿqilūna in hum illā kal-anʿāmi bal hum aḍallu sabīlan

tr.85: Do you think that most of them hear or understand? They are just like cattle- no, they are further from the path.
tr.19: Or deemest thou that most of them hear or understand? They are but as the cattle - nay, but they are farther astray?
tr.22: Or thinkest thou that most of them listen or understand? They are only like cattle;- nay, they are worse astray in Path.
tr.203: Or do you think that most of them hear or understand? They are only like cattle - nay, they are even farther astray from the Path (i.e. even worse than cattle).

25.ar: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ وَلَوْ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُۥ سَاكِنًا ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا ٱلشَّمْسَ عَلَيْهِ دَلِيلًا
25.en: Have you not considered your Lord - how He extends the shadow, and if He willed, He could have made it stationary? Then We made the sun for it an indication.
25.tl: alam tara ilā rabbika kayfa madda l-ẓila walaw shāa lajaʿalahu sākinan thumma jaʿalnā l-shamsa ʿalayhi dalīlan

tr.85: Do you not see how your Lord lengthens the shade? If He had willed, He could have made it stand still- We made the sun its indicator-
tr.19: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord hath spread the shade - And if He willed He could have made it still - then We have made the sun its pilot;
tr.22: Hast thou not turned thy vision to thy Lord?- How He doth prolong the shadow! If He willed, He could make it stationary! then do We make the sun its guide;
tr.203: Have you not seen how your Lord spread the shadow. If He willed, He could have made it still - But We have made the sun its guide (i.e. after the sunrise, the shadow shrinks and vanishes at midnoon and then again appears in the afternoon with the decline of the sun, and had there been no sunlight, there would have been no shadow).

25.ar: ثُمَّ قَبَضْنَـٰهُ إِلَيْنَا قَبْضًا يَسِيرًا
25.en: Then We [retract and] hold it with Us for a brief grasp.
25.tl: thumma qabaḍnāhu ilaynā qabḍan yasīran

tr.85: but We gradually draw it towards Us, little by little.
tr.19: Then We withdraw it unto Us, a gradual withdrawal?
tr.22: Then We draw it in towards Ourselves,- a contraction by easy stages.
tr.203: Then We withdraw it to Us a gradual concealed withdrawal.

25.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَٱلنَّوْمَ سُبَاتًا وَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ نُشُورًا
25.en: And it is He who has made the night for you as clothing and sleep [a means for] rest and has made the day a resurrection.
25.tl: wahuwa alladhī jaʿala lakumu al-layla libāsan wal-nawma subātan wajaʿala l-nahāra nushūran

tr.85: It is He who made the night a garment for you, and sleep a rest, and made the day like a resurrection.
tr.19: And He it is Who maketh night a covering for you, and sleep repose, and maketh day a resurrection.
tr.22: And He it is Who makes the Night as a Robe for you, and Sleep as Repose, and makes the Day (as it were) a Resurrection.
tr.203: And it is He Who makes the night a covering for you, and the sleep (as) a repose, and makes the day Nushûr (i.e. getting up and going about here and there for daily work, after one’s sleep at night, or like resurrection after one’s death).

25.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَرْسَلَ ٱلرِّيَـٰحَ بُشْرًۢا بَيْنَ يَدَىْ رَحْمَتِهِۦ ۚ وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً طَهُورًا
25.en: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy [i.e., rainfall], and We send down from the sky pure water
25.tl: wahuwa alladhī arsala l-riyāḥa bush'ran bayna yaday raḥmatihi wa-anzalnā mina l-samāi māan ṭahūran

tr.85: It is He who sends the winds as heralds of good news before His Mercy. We send down pure water from the sky,
tr.19: And He it is Who sendeth the winds, glad tidings heralding His mercy, and We send down purifying water from the sky,
tr.22: And He it is Who sends the winds as heralds of glad tidings, going before His mercy, and We send down pure water from the sky,-
tr.203: And it is He Who sends the winds as heralds of glad tidings, going before His Mercy (rain); and We send down pure water from the sky.

25.ar: لِّنُحْـِۧىَ بِهِۦ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتًا وَنُسْقِيَهُۥ مِمَّا خَلَقْنَآ أَنْعَـٰمًا وَأَنَاسِىَّ كَثِيرًا
25.en: That We may bring to life thereby a dead land and give it as drink to those We created of numerous livestock and men.
25.tl: linuḥ'yiya bihi baldatan maytan wanus'qiyahu mimmā khalaqnā anʿāman wa-anāsiyya kathīran

tr.85: so that We can revive a dead land with it, and We give it as a drink to many animals and people We have created.
tr.19: That We may give life thereby to a dead land, and We give many beasts and men that We have created to drink thereof.
tr.22: That with it We may give life to a dead land, and slake the thirst of things We have created,- cattle and men in great numbers.
tr.203: That We may give life thereby to a dead land, and We give to drink thereof many of the cattle and men that We had created.

25.ar: وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَـٰهُ بَيْنَهُمْ لِيَذَّكَّرُوا۟ فَأَبَىٰٓ أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُورًا
25.en: And We have certainly distributed it among them that they might be reminded, but most of the people refuse except disbelief.
25.tl: walaqad ṣarrafnāhu baynahum liyadhakkarū fa-abā aktharu l-nāsi illā kufūran

tr.85: Many times We have repeated this to people so that they might take heed, but most persist in their ingratitude.
tr.19: And verily We have repeated it among them that they may remember, but most of mankind begrudge aught save ingratitude.
tr.22: And We have distributed the (water) amongst them, in order that they may celebrate (our) praises, but most men are averse (to aught) but (rank) ingratitude.
tr.203: And indeed We have distributed it (rain or water) amongst them in order that they may remember (the Grace of Allâh,) but most men (refuse to accept the Truth or Faith and) accept nothing but disbelief or ingratitude.

25.ar: وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَبَعَثْنَا فِى كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ نَّذِيرًا
25.en: And if We had willed, We could have sent into every city a warner.
25.tl: walaw shi'nā labaʿathnā fī kulli qaryatin nadhīran

tr.85: If it had been Our will, We would have sent a warner to every town,
tr.19: If We willed, We could raise up a warner in every village.
tr.22: Had it been Our Will, We could have sent a warner to every centre of population.
tr.203: And had We willed, We would have raised a warner in every town.

25.ar: فَلَا تُطِعِ ٱلْكَـٰفِرِينَ وَجَـٰهِدْهُم بِهِۦ جِهَادًا كَبِيرًا
25.en: So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it [i.e., the Qur’ān] a great striving.
25.tl: falā tuṭiʿi l-kāfirīna wajāhid'hum bihi jihādan kabīran

tr.85: so do not give in to the disbelievers: strive hard against them with this Quran.
tr.19: So obey not the disbelievers, but strive against them herewith with a great endeavour.
tr.22: Therefore listen not to the Unbelievers, but strive against them with the utmost strenuousness, with the (Qur'an).
tr.203: So obey not the disbelievers, but strive against them (by preaching) with the utmost endeavour with it (the Qur’ân).

25.ar: ۞ وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ هَـٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ وَهَـٰذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخًا وَحِجْرًا مَّحْجُورًا
25.en: And it is He who has released [simultaneously] the two seas [i.e., bodies of water], one fresh and sweet and one salty and bitter, and He placed between them a barrier and prohibiting partition.
25.tl: wahuwa alladhī maraja l-baḥrayni hādhā ʿadhbun furātun wahādhā mil'ḥun ujājun wajaʿala baynahumā barzakhan waḥij'ran maḥjūran

tr.85: It is He who released the two bodies of flowing water, one sweet and fresh and the other salty and bitter, and put an insurmountable barrier between them.
tr.19: And He it is Who hath given independence to the two seas (though they meet); one palatable, sweet, and the other saltish, bitter; and hath set a bar and a forbidding ban between them.
tr.22: It is He Who has let free the two bodies of flowing water: One palatable and sweet, and the other salt and bitter; yet has He made a barrier between them, a partition that is forbidden to be passed.
tr.203: And it is He Who has let free the two seas (kinds of water): this is palatable and sweet, and that is salt and bitter; and He has set a barrier and a complete partition between them.

25.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ بَشَرًا فَجَعَلَهُۥ نَسَبًا وَصِهْرًا ۗ وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ قَدِيرًا
25.en: And it is He who has created from water [i.e., semen] a human being and made him [a relative by] lineage and marriage. And ever is your Lord competent [concerning creation].
25.tl: wahuwa alladhī khalaqa mina l-māi basharan fajaʿalahu nasaban waṣih'ran wakāna rabbuka qadīran

tr.85: It is He who creates human beings from fluid, then makes them kin by blood and marriage: your Lord is all powerful!
tr.19: And He it is Who hath created man from water, and hath appointed for him kindred by blood and kindred by marriage; for thy Lord is ever Powerful.
tr.22: It is He Who has created man from water: then has He established relationships of lineage and marriage: for thy Lord has power (over all things).
tr.203: And it is He Who has created man from water, and has appointed for him kindred by blood, and kindred by marriage. And your Lord is Ever All-Powerful to do what He wills.

25.ar: وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنفَعُهُمْ وَلَا يَضُرُّهُمْ ۗ وَكَانَ ٱلْكَافِرُ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ ظَهِيرًا
25.en: But they worship rather than Allāh that which does not benefit them or harm them, and the disbeliever is ever, against his Lord, an assistant [to Satan].
25.tl: wayaʿbudūna min dūni l-lahi mā lā yanfaʿuhum walā yaḍurruhum wakāna l-kāfiru ʿalā rabbihi ẓahīran

tr.85: Yet instead of God they worship things that can neither benefit nor harm them: the disbeliever has always turned his back on his Lord.
tr.19: Yet they worship instead of Allah that which can neither benefit them nor hurt them. The disbeliever was ever a partisan against his Lord.
tr.22: Yet do they worship, besides Allah, things that can neither profit them nor harm them: and the Misbeliever is a helper (of Evil), against his own Lord!
tr.203: And they (disbelievers, polytheists) worship besides Allâh that which can neither profit them nor harm them; and the disbeliever is ever a helper (of the Satan) against his Lord.

25.ar: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَـٰكَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرًا وَنَذِيرًا
25.en: And We have not sent you, [O Muḥammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
25.tl: wamā arsalnāka illā mubashiran wanadhīran

tr.85: We sent you only to give good news and warning.
tr.19: And We have sent thee (O Muhammad) only as a bearer of good tidings and a warner.
tr.22: But thee We only sent to give glad tidings and admonition.
tr.203: And We have sent you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) only as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner.

25.ar: قُلْ مَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِلَّا مَن شَآءَ أَن يَتَّخِذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ سَبِيلًا
25.en: Say, "I do not ask of you for it any payment - only that whoever wills might take to his Lord a way."
25.tl: qul mā asalukum ʿalayhi min ajrin illā man shāa an yattakhidha ilā rabbihi sabīlan

tr.85: Say, ‘I am not asking for any reward for it, but anyone who wishes should take a path to his Lord.’
tr.19: Say: I ask of you no reward for this, save that whoso will may choose a way unto his Lord.
tr.22: Say: "No reward do I ask of you for it but this: that each one who will may take a (straight) Path to his Lord."
tr.203: Say: "No reward do I ask of you for this (that which I have brought from my Lord and its preaching), save that whosoever wills may take a Path to his Lord.

25.ar: وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱلْحَىِّ ٱلَّذِى لَا يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِهِۦ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِۦ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرًا
25.en: And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt [Allāh] with His praise. And sufficient is He to be, with the sins of His servants, [fully] Aware -
25.tl: watawakkal ʿalā l-ḥayi alladhī lā yamūtu wasabbiḥ biḥamdihi wakafā bihi bidhunūbi ʿibādihi khabīran

tr.85: Put your trust in the Living [God] who never dies, and celebrate His praise. He knows the sins of His servants well enough:
tr.19: And trust thou in the Living One Who dieth not, and hymn His praise. He sufficeth as the Knower of His bondmen's sins,
tr.22: And put thy trust in Him Who lives and dies not; and celebrate his praise; and enough is He to be acquainted with the faults of His servants;-
tr.203: And put your trust (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) in the Ever Living One Who dies not, and glorify His Praises, and Sufficient is He as the All-Knower of the sins of His slaves,

25.ar: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِى سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلْعَرْشِ ۚ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ فَسْـَٔلْ بِهِۦ خَبِيرًا
25.en: He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days and then established Himself above the Throne - the Most Merciful, so ask about Him one well informed [i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ)].
25.tl: alladhī khalaqa l-samāwāti wal-arḍa wamā baynahumā fī sittati ayyāmin thumma is'tawā ʿalā l-ʿarshi l-raḥmānu fasal bihi khabīran

tr.85: it is He who created the heavens and earth and what is between them in six Days, and then established Himself on the throne- He is the Lord of Mercy; He is the Best Informed.
tr.19: Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six Days, then He mounted the Throne. The Beneficent! Ask anyone informed concerning Him!
tr.22: He Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between, in six days, and is firmly established on the Throne (of Authority): Allah Most Gracious: ask thou, then, about Him of any acquainted (with such things).
tr.203: Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six Days. Then He (Istawâ ) rose over the Throne (in a manner that suits His Majesty). The Most Gracious (Allâh)! Ask Him (O Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم , concerning His Qualities: His rising over His Throne, His creations, etc.), as He is Al-Khabîr (The All-Knower of everything i.e. Allâh).

25.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ قَالُوا۟ وَمَا ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ أَنَسْجُدُ لِمَا تَأْمُرُنَا وَزَادَهُمْ نُفُورًا ۩
25.en: And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Should we prostrate to that which you order us?" And it increases them in aversion.
25.tl: wa-idhā qīla lahumu us'judū lilrraḥmāni qālū wamā l-raḥmānu anasjudu limā tamurunā wazādahum nufūran

tr.85: Yet when they are told, ‘Bow down before the Lord of Mercy,’ they say, ‘What is the Lord of Mercy? Should we bow down before anything you command?’ and they turn even further away.
tr.19: And when it is said unto them: Prostrate to the Beneficent! they say: And what is the Beneficent? Are we to prostrate to whatever thou (Muhammad) biddest us? And it increaseth aversion in them.
tr.22: When it is said to them, "Prostrate to (Allah) Most Gracious!", they say, "And what is (Allah) Most Gracious? Shall we prostrate to that which thou commandest us?" And it increases their flight (from the Truth).
tr.203: And when it is said to them: "Prostrate yourselves to the Most Gracious (Allâh)! they say: "And what is the Most Gracious? Shall we fall down in prostration to that which you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) command us?" And it increases in them only aversion.

25.ar: تَبَارَكَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ بُرُوجًا وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَٰجًا وَقَمَرًا مُّنِيرًا
25.en: Blessed is He who has placed in the sky great stars and placed therein a [burning] lamp and luminous moon.
25.tl: tabāraka alladhī jaʿala fī l-samāi burūjan wajaʿala fīhā sirājan waqamaran munīran

tr.85: Exalted is He who put constellations in the heavens, a radiant light, and an illuminating moon-
tr.19: Blessed be He Who hath placed in the heaven mansions of the stars, and hath placed therein a great lamp and a moon giving light!
tr.22: Blessed is He Who made constellations in the skies, and placed therein a Lamp and a Moon giving light;
tr.203: Blessed be He Who has placed in the heaven big stars, and has placed therein a great lamp (sun), and a moon giving light.

25.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ خِلْفَةً لِّمَنْ أَرَادَ أَن يَذَّكَّرَ أَوْ أَرَادَ شُكُورًا
25.en: And it is He who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude.
25.tl: wahuwa alladhī jaʿala al-layla wal-nahāra khil'fatan liman arāda an yadhakkara aw arāda shukūran

tr.85: it is He who made the night and day follow each other- so anyone who wishes may be mindful or show gratitude.
tr.19: And He it is Who hath appointed night and day in succession, for him who desireth to remember, or desireth thankfulness.
tr.22: And it is He Who made the Night and the Day to follow each other: for such as have the will to celebrate His praises or to show their gratitude.
tr.203: And He it is Who has put the night and the day in succession, for such who desires to remember or desires to show his gratitude.

25.ar: وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ ٱلْجَـٰهِلُونَ قَالُوا۟ سَلَـٰمًا
25.en: And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth easily, and when the ignorant address them [harshly], they say [words of] peace,
25.tl: waʿibādu l-raḥmāni alladhīna yamshūna ʿalā l-arḍi hawnan wa-idhā khāṭabahumu l-jāhilūna qālū salāman

tr.85: The servants of the Lord of Mercy are those who walk humbly on the earth, and who, when the foolish address them, reply, ‘Peace’;
tr.19: The (faithful) slaves of the Beneficent are they who walk upon the earth modestly, and when the foolish ones address them answer: Peace;
tr.22: And the servants of (Allah) Most Gracious are those who walk on the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace!";
tr.203: And the (faithful) slaves of the Most Gracious (Allâh) are those who walk on the earth in humility and sedateness, and when the foolish address them (with bad words) they reply back with mild words of gentleness.

25.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَقِيَـٰمًا
25.en: And those who spend [part of] the night to their Lord prostrating and standing [in prayer]
25.tl: wa-alladhīna yabītūna lirabbihim sujjadan waqiyāman

tr.85: those who spend the night bowed down or standing, worshipping their Lord,
tr.19: And who spend the night before their Lord, prostrate and standing,
tr.22: Those who spend the night in adoration of their Lord prostrate and standing;
tr.203: And those who spend the night in worship of their Lord, prostrate and standing.

25.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا ٱصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَ ۖ إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَامًا
25.en: And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell. Indeed, its punishment is ever adhering;
25.tl: wa-alladhīna yaqūlūna rabbanā iṣ'rif ʿannā ʿadhāba jahannama inna ʿadhābahā kāna gharāman

tr.85: who plead, ‘Our Lord, turn away from us the suffering of Hell, for it is a dreadful torment to suffer!
tr.19: And who say: Our Lord! Avert from us the doom of hell; lo! the doom thereof is anguish;
tr.22: Those who say, "Our Lord! avert from us the Wrath of Hell, for its Wrath is indeed an affliction grievous,-
tr.203: And those who say: "Our Lord! Avert from us the torment of Hell. Verily its torment is ever an inseparable, permanent punishment."

25.ar: إِنَّهَا سَآءَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا
25.en: Indeed, it is evil as a settlement and residence."
25.tl: innahā sāat mus'taqarran wamuqāman

tr.85: It is an evil home, a foul resting place!’
tr.19: Lo! it is wretched as abode and station;
tr.22: "Evil indeed is it as an abode, and as a place to rest in";
tr.203: Evil indeed it (Hell) is as an abode and as a place to rest in.

25.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَنفَقُوا۟ لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا۟ وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا۟ وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ قَوَامًا
25.en: And [they are] those who, when they spend, do so not excessively or sparingly but are ever, between that, [justly] moderate
25.tl: wa-alladhīna idhā anfaqū lam yus'rifū walam yaqturū wakāna bayna dhālika qawāman

tr.85: They are those who are neither wasteful nor niggardly when they spend, but keep to a just balance;
tr.19: And those who, when they spend, are neither prodigal nor grudging; and there is ever a firm station between the two;
tr.22: Those who, when they spend, are not extravagant and not niggardly, but hold a just (balance) between those (extremes);
tr.203: And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor niggardly, but hold a medium (way) between those (extremes).

25.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَـٰهًا ءَاخَرَ وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفْسَ ٱلَّتِى حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ وَلَا يَزْنُونَ ۚ وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَامًا
25.en: And those who do not invoke with Allāh another deity or kill the soul which Allāh has forbidden [to be killed], except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever should do that will meet a penalty.
25.tl: wa-alladhīna lā yadʿūna maʿa l-lahi ilāhan ākhara walā yaqtulūna l-nafsa allatī ḥarrama l-lahu illā bil-ḥaqi walā yaznūna waman yafʿal dhālika yalqa athāman

tr.85: those who never invoke any other deity beside God, nor take a life, which God has made sacred, except in the pursuit of justice, nor commit adultery. (Whoever does these things will face the penalties:
tr.19: And those who cry not unto any other god along with Allah, nor take the life which Allah hath forbidden save in (course of) justice, nor commit adultery - and whoso doeth this shall pay the penalty;
tr.22: Those who invoke not, with Allah, any other god, nor slay such life as Allah has made sacred except for just cause, nor commit fornication; - and any that does this (not only) meets punishment.
tr.203: And those who invoke not any other ilâh (god) along with Allâh, nor kill such person as Allâh has forbidden, except for just cause, nor commit illegal sexual intercourse - and whoever does this shall receive the punishment.

25.ar: يُضَـٰعَفْ لَهُ ٱلْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِۦ مُهَانًا
25.en: Multiplied for him is the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated -
25.tl: yuḍāʿaf lahu l-ʿadhābu yawma l-qiyāmati wayakhlud fīhi muhānan

tr.85: their torment will be doubled on the Day of Resurrection, and they will remain in torment, disgraced,
tr.19: The doom will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein disdained for ever;
tr.22: (But) the Penalty on the Day of Judgment will be doubled to him, and he will dwell therein in ignominy,-
tr.203: The torment will be doubled to him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in disgrace;

25.ar: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صَـٰلِحًا فَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمْ حَسَنَـٰتٍ ۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا
25.en: Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work. For them Allāh will replace their evil deeds with good. And ever is Allāh Forgiving and Merciful.
25.tl: illā man tāba waāmana waʿamila ʿamalan ṣāliḥan fa-ulāika yubaddilu l-lahu sayyiātihim ḥasanātin wakāna l-lahu ghafūran raḥīman

tr.85: except those who repent, believe, and do good deeds: God will change the evil deeds of such people into good ones. He is most forgiving, most merciful.
tr.19: Save him who repenteth and believeth and doth righteous work; as for such, Allah will change their evil deeds to good deeds. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful.
tr.22: Unless he repents, believes, and works righteous deeds, for Allah will change the evil of such persons into good, and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful,
tr.203: Except those who repent and believe (in Islâmic Monotheism), and do righteous deeds; for those, Allâh will change their sins into good deeds, and Allâh is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

25.ar: وَمَن تَابَ وَعَمِلَ صَـٰلِحًا فَإِنَّهُۥ يَتُوبُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَتَابًا
25.en: And he who repents and does righteousness does indeed turn to Allāh with [accepted] repentance.
25.tl: waman tāba waʿamila ṣāliḥan fa-innahu yatūbu ilā l-lahi matāban

tr.85: People who repent and do good deeds truly return to God.)
tr.19: And whosoever repenteth and doeth good, he verily repenteth toward Allah with true repentance -
tr.22: And whoever repents and does good has truly turned to Allah with an (acceptable) conversion;-
tr.203: And whosoever repents and does righteous good deeds; then verily, he repents towards Allâh with true repentance.

25.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ ٱلزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّوا۟ بِٱللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا۟ كِرَامًا
25.en: And [they are] those who do not testify to falsehood, and when they pass near ill speech, they pass by with dignity.
25.tl: wa-alladhīna lā yashhadūna l-zūra wa-idhā marrū bil-laghwi marrū kirāman

tr.85: [The servants of the Lord of Mercy are] those who do not give false testimony, and who, when they see some frivolity, pass by with dignity;
tr.19: And those who will not witness vanity, but when they pass near senseless play, pass by with dignity.
tr.22: Those who witness no falsehood, and, if they pass by futility, they pass by it with honourable (avoidance);
tr.203: And those who do not bear witness to falsehood, and if they pass by some evil play or evil talk, they pass by it with dignity.

25.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَـٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَمْ يَخِرُّوا۟ عَلَيْهَا صُمًّا وَعُمْيَانًا
25.en: And those who, when reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind.
25.tl: wa-alladhīna idhā dhukkirū biāyāti rabbihim lam yakhirrū ʿalayhā ṣumman waʿum'yānan

tr.85: who, when reminded of their Lord’s signs, do not turn a deaf ear and a blind eye to them;
tr.19: And those who, when they are reminded of the revelations of their Lord, fall not deaf and blind thereat.
tr.22: Those who, when they are admonished with the Signs of their Lord, droop not down at them as if they were deaf or blind;
tr.203: And those who, when they are reminded of the Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) of their Lord, fall not deaf and blind thereat.

25.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَٰجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّـٰتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَٱجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
25.en: And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us a leader [i.e., example] for the righteous."
25.tl: wa-alladhīna yaqūlūna rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā wadhurriyyātinā qurrata aʿyunin wa-ij'ʿalnā lil'muttaqīna imāman

tr.85: those who pray, ‘Our Lord, give us joy in our spouses and offspring. Make us good examples to those who are aware of You’.
tr.19: And who say: Our Lord! Vouchsafe us comfort of our wives and of our offspring, and make us patterns for (all) those who ward off (evil).
tr.22: And those who pray, "Our Lord! Grant unto us wives and offspring who will be the comfort of our eyes, and give us (the grace) to lead the righteous."
tr.203: And those who say: "Our Lord! Bestow on us from our wives and our offspring the comfort of our eyes, and make us leaders of the Muttaqûn(the pious. See V.2:2)."

25.ar: أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ ٱلْغُرْفَةَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا۟ وَيُلَقَّوْنَ فِيهَا تَحِيَّةً وَسَلَـٰمًا
25.en: Those will be awarded the Chamber for what they patiently endured, and they will be received therein with greetings and [words of] peace,
25.tl: ulāika yuj'zawna l-ghur'fata bimā ṣabarū wayulaqqawna fīhā taḥiyyatan wasalāman

tr.85: These servants will be rewarded with the highest place in Paradise for their steadfastness. There they will be met with greetings and peace.
tr.19: They will be awarded the high place forasmuch as they were steadfast, and they will meet therein with welcome and the ward of peace,
tr.22: Those are the ones who will be rewarded with the highest place in heaven, because of their patient constancy: therein shall they be met with salutations and peace,
tr.203: Those will be rewarded with the highest place (in Paradise) because of their patience. Therein they shall be met with greetings and the word of peace and respect.

25.ar: خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا ۚ حَسُنَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا
25.en: Abiding eternally therein. Good is the settlement and residence.
25.tl: khālidīna fīhā ḥasunat mus'taqarran wamuqāman

tr.85: There they will stay- a happy home and resting place!
tr.19: Abiding there for ever. Happy is it as abode and station!
tr.22: Dwelling therein;- how beautiful an abode and place of rest!
tr.203: Abiding therein - excellent it is as an abode, and as a place to rest in.

25.ar: قُلْ مَا يَعْبَؤُا۟ بِكُمْ رَبِّى لَوْلَا دُعَآؤُكُمْ ۖ فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزَامًۢا
25.en: Say, "What would my Lord care for you if not for your supplication?" For you [disbelievers] have denied, so it [i.e., your denial] is going to be adherent.
25.tl: qul mā yaʿba-u bikum rabbī lawlā duʿāukum faqad kadhabtum fasawfa yakūnu lizāman

tr.85: [Prophet, tell the disbelievers], ‘What are you to my Lord without your supplication? But since you have written offthe truth as lies, the inevitable will happen.’
tr.19: Say (O Muhammad, unto the disbelievers): My Lord would not concern Himself with you but for your prayer. But now ye have denied (the Truth), therefor there will be judgment.
tr.22: Say (to the Rejecters): "My Lord is not uneasy because of you if ye call not on Him: But ye have indeed rejected (Him), and soon will come the inevitable (punishment)!"
tr.203: Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم to the disbelievers): "My Lord pays attention to you only because of your invocation to Him. But now you have indeed denied (Him). So the torment will be yours for ever (inseparable, permanent punishment)."

26.en: Ṭā, Seen, Meem.

tr.85: Ta Sin Mim
tr.19: Ta. Sin. Mim.
tr.22: Ta. Sin. Mim.
tr.203: Tâ-Sîn-Mîm.

26.en: These are the verses of the clear Book.

tr.85: These are the verses of the Scripture that makes things clear:
tr.19: These are revelations of the Scripture that maketh plain.
tr.22: These are verses of the Book that makes (things) clear.
tr.203: These are the Verses of the manifest Book [(this Qur’ân), which was promised by Allâh in the Taurât (Torah) and the Injeel (Gospel), makes things clear].

26.ar: لَعَلَّكَ بَـٰخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُوا۟ مُؤْمِنِينَ
26.en: Perhaps, [O Muḥammad], you would kill yourself with grief that they will not be believers.
26.tl: laʿallaka bākhiʿun nafsaka allā yakūnū mu'minīna

tr.85: [Prophet], are you going to worry yourself to death because they will not believe?
tr.19: It may be that thou tormentest thyself (O Muhammad) because they believe not.
tr.22: It may be thou frettest thy soul with grief, that they do not become Believers.
tr.203: It may be that you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) are going to kill yourself with grief, that they do not become believers [in your Risalah (Messengership) i.e. in your Message of Islâmic Monotheism].

26.ar: إِن نَّشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ ءَايَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَـٰقُهُمْ لَهَا خَـٰضِعِينَ
26.en: If We willed, We could send down to them from the sky a sign for which their necks would remain humbled.
26.tl: in nasha nunazzil ʿalayhim mina l-samāi āyatan faẓallat aʿnāquhum lahā khāḍiʿīna

tr.85: If We had wished, We could have sent them down a sign from heaven, at which their necks would stay bowed in utter humility.
tr.19: If We will, We can send down on them from the sky a portent so that their necks would remain bowed before it.
tr.22: If (such) were Our Will, We could send down to them from the sky a Sign, to which they would bend their necks in humility.
tr.203: If We will, We could send down to them from the heaven a sign, to which they would bend their necks in humility.

26.ar: وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّنَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا۟ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضِينَ
26.en: And no mention [i.e., revelation] comes to them anew from the Most Merciful except that they turn away from it.
26.tl: wamā yatīhim min dhik'rin mina l-raḥmāni muḥ'dathin illā kānū ʿanhu muʿ'riḍīna

tr.85: Whenever they are brought a new revelation from the Lord of Mercy, they turn away:
tr.19: Never cometh there unto them a fresh reminder from the Beneficent One, but they turn away from it.
tr.22: But there comes not to them a newly-revealed Message from (Allah) Most Gracious, but they turn away therefrom.
tr.203: And never comes there unto them a Reminder as a recent revelation from the Most Gracious (Allâh), but they turn away therefrom.

26.ar: فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوا۟ فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أَنۢبَـٰٓؤُا۟ مَا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
26.en: For they have already denied, but there will come to them the news of that which they used to ridicule.
26.tl: faqad kadhabū fasayatīhim anbāu mā kānū bihi yastahziūna

tr.85: they deny it, but the truth of what they scorned will soon hit them.
tr.19: Now they have denied (the Truth); but there will come unto them tidings of that whereat they used to scoff.
tr.22: They have indeed rejected (the Message): so they will know soon (enough) the truth of what they mocked at!
tr.203: So they have indeed denied (the truth - this Qur’ân), then the news of what they mocked at will come to them.

26.ar: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنۢبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ
26.en: Did they not look at the earth - how much We have produced therein from every noble kind?
26.tl: awalam yaraw ilā l-arḍi kam anbatnā fīhā min kulli zawjin karīmin

tr.85: Do they not see the earth, and what noble kinds of thing We grow in it?
tr.19: Have they not seen the earth, how much of every fruitful kind We make to grow therein?
tr.22: Do they not look at the earth,- how many noble things of all kinds We have produced therein?
tr.203: Do they not observe the earth - how much of every good kind We cause to grow therein?

26.ar: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَةً ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
26.en: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
26.tl: inna fī dhālika laāyatan wamā kāna aktharuhum mu'minīna

tr.85: There truly is a sign in this, though most of them do not believe:
tr.19: Lo! herein is indeed a portent; yet most of them are not believers.
tr.22: Verily, in this is a Sign: but most of them do not believe.
tr.203: Verily, in this is an Ayâh (proof or sign), yet most of them (polytheists, pagans who do not believe in Resurrection) are not believers.

26.en: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

tr.85: your Lord alone is the Almighty, the Merciful.
tr.19: And lo! thy Lord! He is indeed the Mighty, the Merciful.
tr.22: And verily, thy Lord is He, the Exalted in Might, Most Merciful.
tr.203: And verily your Lord, He is truly the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful.

26.ar: وَإِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبُّكَ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنِ ٱئْتِ ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ
26.en: And [mention] when your Lord called Moses, [saying], "Go to the wrongdoing people -
26.tl: wa-idh nādā rabbuka mūsā ani i'ti l-qawma l-ẓālimīna

tr.85: Your Lord called to Moses: ‘Go to those wrongdoers,
tr.19: And when thy Lord called Moses, saying: Go unto the wrongdoing folk,
tr.22: Behold, thy Lord called Moses: "Go to the people of iniquity,-
tr.203: And (remember) when your Lord called Mûsâ (Moses) (saying): "Go to the people who are Zâlimûn (polytheists and wrong-doers) -

26.en: The people of Pharaoh. Will they not fear Allāh?"

tr.85: the people of Pharaoh. Will they not take heed?’
tr.19: The folk of Pharaoh. Will they not ward off (evil)?
tr.22: "The people of the Pharaoh: will they not fear Allah?"
tr.203: "The people of Fir‘aun (Pharaoh): Will they not fear Allâh and become righteous?"

26.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
26.en: He said, "My Lord, indeed I fear that they will deny me
26.tl: qāla rabbi innī akhāfu an yukadhibūni

tr.85: Moses said, ‘My Lord, I fear they will call me a liar,
tr.19: He said: My Lord! Lo! I fear that they will deny me,
tr.22: He said: "O my Lord! I do fear that they will charge me with falsehood:
tr.203: He said: "My Lord! Verily, I fear that they will belie me,

26.ar: وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَـٰرُونَ
26.en: And that my breast will tighten and my tongue will not be fluent, so send for Aaron.
26.tl: wayaḍīqu ṣadrī walā yanṭaliqu lisānī fa-arsil ilā hārūna

tr.85: and I will feel stressed and tongue-tied, so send Aaron too;
tr.19: And I shall be embarrassed, and my tongue will not speak plainly, therefor send for Aaron (to help me).
tr.22: "My breast will be straitened. And my speech may not go (smoothly): so send unto Aaron.
tr.203: "And my breast straitens, and my tongue expresses not well. So send for Hârûn (Aaron) (to come along with me).

26.ar: وَلَهُمْ عَلَىَّ ذَنۢبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
26.en: And they have upon me a [claim due to] sin, so I fear that they will kill me."
26.tl: walahum ʿalayya dhanbun fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni

tr.85: besides, they have a chargeagainst me, and I fear they may kill me.’
tr.19: And they have a crime against me, so I fear that they will kill me.
tr.22: "And (further), they have a charge of crime against me; and I fear they may slay me."
tr.203: "And they have a charge of crime against me, and I fear they will kill me."

26.ar: قَالَ كَلَّا ۖ فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَآ ۖ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ
26.en: [Allāh] said, "No. Go both of you with Our signs; indeed, We are with you, listening.
26.tl: qāla kallā fa-idh'habā biāyātinā innā maʿakum mus'tamiʿūna

tr.85: God said, ‘No [they will not]. Go, both of you, with Our signs––We shall be with you, listen-ing.
tr.19: He said: Nay, verily. So go ye twain with Our tokens. Lo! We shall be with you, Hearing.
tr.22: Allah said: "By no means! proceed then, both of you, with Our Signs; We are with you, and will listen (to your call).
tr.203: (Allâh) said: "Nay! Go you both with Our Signs. Verily We shall be with you, listening.

26.ar: فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَآ إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ
26.en: Go to Pharaoh and say, 'We are the messengers of the Lord of the worlds,
26.tl: fatiyā fir'ʿawna faqūlā innā rasūlu rabbi l-ʿālamīna

tr.85: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh and say, “We bring a message from the Lord of the Worlds:
tr.19: And come together unto Pharaoh and say: Lo! we bear a message of the Lord of the Worlds,
tr.22: "So go forth, both of you, to Pharaoh, and say: 'We have been sent by the Lord and Cherisher of the worlds;
tr.203: "And go both of you to Fir‘aun (Pharaoh), and say: ‘We are the Messengers of the Lord of the ‘Âlamîn (mankind, jinn and all that exists),

26.en: [Commanded to say], "Send with us the Children of Israel."'"

tr.85: let the Children of Israel leave with us.” ’
tr.19: (Saying): Let the Children of Israel go with us.
tr.22: "'Send thou with us the Children of Israel.'"
tr.203: "So allow the Children of Israel to go with us.’ "

26.ar: قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ
26.en: [Pharaoh] said, "Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life?
26.tl: qāla alam nurabbika fīnā walīdan walabith'ta fīnā min ʿumurika sinīna

tr.85: Pharaoh said, ‘Did we not bring you up as a child among us? Did you not stay with us for many years?
tr.19: (Pharaoh) said (unto Moses): Did we not rear thee among us as a child? And thou didst dwell many years of thy life among us,
tr.22: (Pharaoh) said: "Did we not cherish thee as a child among us, and didst thou not stay in our midst many years of thy life?
tr.203: [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said [to Mûsâ (Moses)]: "Did we not bring you up among us as a child? And you did dwell many years of your life with us.

26.ar: وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ ٱلَّتِى فَعَلْتَ وَأَنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَـٰفِرِينَ
26.en: And [then] you did your deed which you did, and you were of the ungrateful."
26.tl: wafaʿalta faʿlataka allatī faʿalta wa-anta mina l-kāfirīna

tr.85: And then you committed that crime of yours: you were so ungrateful.’
tr.19: And thou didst that thy deed which thou didst, and thou wast one of the ingrates.
tr.22: "And thou didst a deed of thine which (thou knowest) thou didst, and thou art an ungrateful (wretch)!"
tr.203: "And you did your deed, which you did (i.e. the crime of killing a man) while you were one of the ingrates."

26.ar: قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَآ إِذًا وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
26.en: [Moses] said, "I did it, then, while I was of those astray [i.e., ignorant].
26.tl: qāla faʿaltuhā idhan wa-anā mina l-ḍālīna

tr.85: Moses replied, ‘I was misguided when I did it
tr.19: He said: I did it then, when I was of those who are astray.
tr.22: Moses said: "I did it then, when I was in error.
tr.203: Mûsâ (Moses) said: "I did it then, when I was ignorant (as regards my Lord and His Message).

26.ar: فَفَرَرْتُ مِنكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِى رَبِّى حُكْمًا وَجَعَلَنِى مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ
26.en: So I fled from you when I feared you. Then my Lord granted me judgement [i.e., wisdom and prophet hood] and appointed me [as one] of the messengers.
26.tl: fafarartu minkum lammā khif'tukum fawahaba lī rabbī ḥuk'man wajaʿalanī mina l-mur'salīna

tr.85: and I fled from you in fear; later my Lord gave me wisdom and made me one of His messengers.
tr.19: Then I fled from you when I feared you, and my Lord vouchsafed me a command and appointed me (of the number) of those sent (by Him).
tr.22: "So I fled from you (all) when I feared you; but my Lord has (since) invested me with judgment (and wisdom) and appointed me as one of the messengers.
tr.203: "So I fled from you when I feared you. But my Lord has granted me Hukm (i.e. religious knowledge, right judgement of the affairs and Prophethood), and made me one of the Messengers.

26.ar: وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَىَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
26.en: And is this a favor of which you remind me - that you have enslaved the Children of Israel?"
26.tl: watil'ka niʿ'matun tamunnuhā ʿalayya an ʿabbadtta banī is'rāīla

tr.85: And is this- that you have enslaved the Children of Israel- the favour with which you reproach me?’
tr.19: And this is the past favour wherewith thou reproachest me: that thou hast enslaved the Children of Israel.
tr.22: "And this is the favour with which thou dost reproach me,- that thou hast enslaved the Children of Israel!"
tr.203: "And this is the past favour with which you reproach me: that you have enslaved the Children of Israel."

26.en: Said Pharaoh, "And what is the Lord of the worlds?"

tr.85: Pharaoh asked, ‘What is this “Lord of the Worlds”?’
tr.19: Pharaoh said: And what is the Lord of the Worlds?
tr.22: Pharaoh said: "And what is the 'Lord and Cherisher of the worlds'?"
tr.203: Fir‘aun (Pharaoh) said: "And what is the Lord of the ‘Âlamîn (mankind, jinn and all that exists)?"

26.ar: قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ ۖ إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ
26.en: [Moses] said, "The Lord of the heavens and earth and that between them, if you should be convinced."
26.tl: qāla rabbu l-samāwāti wal-arḍi wamā baynahumā in kuntum mūqinīna

tr.85: Moses replied, ‘He is the Lord of the heavens and earth and everything between them. If you would only have faith!’
tr.19: (Moses) said: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, if ye had but sure belief.
tr.22: (Moses) said: "The Lord and Cherisher of the heavens and the earth, and all between,- if ye want to be quite sure."
tr.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, if you seek to be convinced with certainty."

26.en: [Pharaoh] said to those around him, "Do you not hear?"

tr.85: Pharaoh said to those present, ‘Do you hear what he says?’
tr.19: (Pharaoh) said unto those around him: Hear ye not?
tr.22: (Pharaoh) said to those around: "Did ye not listen (to what he says)?"
tr.203: [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said to those around: "Do you not hear (what he says)?"

26.en: [Moses] said, "Your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers."

tr.85: Moses said, ‘He is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.’
tr.19: He said: Your Lord and the Lord of your fathers.
tr.22: (Moses) said: "Your Lord and the Lord of your fathers from the beginning!"
tr.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "Your Lord and the Lord of your ancient fathers!"

26.ar: قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ
26.en: [Pharaoh] said, "Indeed, your 'messenger' who has been sent to you is mad."
26.tl: qāla inna rasūlakumu alladhī ur'sila ilaykum lamajnūnun

tr.85: Pharaoh said, ‘This messenger who has been sent to you is truly possessed.’
tr.19: (Pharaoh) said: Lo! your messenger who hath been sent unto you is indeed a madman!
tr.22: (Pharaoh) said: "Truly your messenger who has been sent to you is a veritable madman!"
tr.203: [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: "Verily, your Messenger who has been sent to you is a madman!"

26.ar: قَالَ رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَآ ۖ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ
26.en: [Moses] said, "Lord of the east and the west and that between them, if you were to reason."
26.tl: qāla rabbu l-mashriqi wal-maghribi wamā baynahumā in kuntum taʿqilūna

tr.85: Moses continued, ‘Lord of the East and West and everything between them. If you would only use your reason!’
tr.19: He said: Lord of the East and the West and all that is between them, if ye did but understand.
tr.22: (Moses) said: "Lord of the East and the West, and all between! if ye only had sense!"
tr.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "Lord of the east and the west, and all that is between them, if you did but understand!"

26.ar: قَالَ لَئِنِ ٱتَّخَذْتَ إِلَـٰهًا غَيْرِى لَأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْمَسْجُونِينَ
26.en: [Pharaoh] said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely place you among those imprisoned."
26.tl: qāla la-ini ittakhadhta ilāhan ghayrī la-ajʿalannaka mina l-masjūnīna

tr.85: But Pharaoh said [to him], ‘If you take any god other than me, I will throw you into prison,’
tr.19: (Pharaoh) said: If thou choosest a god other than me, I assuredly shall place thee among the prisoners.
tr.22: (Pharaoh) said: "If thou dost put forward any god other than me, I will certainly put thee in prison!"
tr.203: [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: "If you choose an ilâh (god) other than me, I will certainly put you among the prisoners."

26.en: [Moses] said, "Even if I brought you something [i.e., proof] manifest?"

tr.85: and Moses asked, ‘Even if I show you something convincing?’
tr.19: He said: Even though I show thee something plain?
tr.22: (Moses) said: "Even if I showed you something clear (and) convincing?"
tr.203: [Mûsâ (Moses)] said: "Even if I bring you something manifest (and convincing)?"

26.ar: قَالَ فَأْتِ بِهِۦٓ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰدِقِينَ
26.en: [Pharaoh] said, "Then bring it, if you should be of the truthful."
26.tl: qāla fati bihi in kunta mina l-ṣādiqīna

tr.85: ‘Show it then,’ said Pharaoh, ‘if you are telling the truth.’
tr.19: (Pharaoh) said: Produce it then, if thou art of the truthful!
tr.22: (Pharaoh) said: "Show it then, if thou tellest the truth!"
tr.203: [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said: "Bring it forth then, if you are of the truthful!"

26.ar: فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ
26.en: So [Moses] threw his staff, and suddenly it was a serpent manifest.
26.tl: fa-alqā ʿaṣāhu fa-idhā hiya thuʿ'bānun mubīnun

tr.85: So Moses threw down his staff and- lo and behold!- it became a snake for everyone to see.
tr.19: Then he flung down his staff and it became a serpent manifest,
tr.22: So (Moses) threw his rod, and behold, it was a serpent, plain (for all to see)!
tr.203: So [Mûsâ (Moses)] threw his stick, and behold, it was a serpent, manifest.

26.ar: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّـٰظِرِينَ
26.en: And he drew out his hand; thereupon it was white for the observers.
26.tl: wanazaʿa yadahu fa-idhā hiya bayḍāu lilnnāẓirīna

tr.85: Then he drew out his hand and- lo and behold!- it was white for the onlookers to see.
tr.19: And he drew forth his hand and lo! it was white to the beholders.
tr.22: And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to all beholders!
tr.203: And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to all beholders!

26.ar: قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُۥٓ إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَسَـٰحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
26.en: [Pharaoh] said to the eminent ones around him, "Indeed, this is a learned magician.
26.tl: qāla lil'mala-i ḥawlahu inna hādhā lasāḥirun ʿalīmun

tr.85: Pharaoh said to the counsellors around him, ‘This man is a learned sorcerer!
tr.19: (Pharaoh) said unto the chiefs about him: Lo! this is verily a knowing wizard,
tr.22: (Pharaoh) said to the Chiefs around him: "This is indeed a sorcerer well-versed:
tr.203: [Fir‘aun (Pharaoh)] said to the chiefs around him: "Verily! This is indeed a well-versed sorcerer.

26.ar: يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِۦ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ
26.en: He wants to drive you out of your land by his magic, so what do you advise?"
26.tl: yurīdu an yukh'rijakum min arḍikum bisiḥ'rihi famādhā tamurūna

tr.85: He means to use his sorcery to drive you out of your land! What do you suggest?’
tr.19: Who would drive you out of your land by his magic. Now what counsel ye?
tr.22: "His plan is to get you out of your land by his sorcery; then what is it ye counsel?"
tr.203: "He wants to drive you out of your land by his sorcery: what is it then that you command?"

26.ar: قَالُوٓا۟ أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَٱبْعَثْ فِى ٱلْمَدَآئِنِ حَـٰشِرِينَ
26.en: They said, "Postpone [the matter of] him and his brother and send among the cities gatherers
26.tl: qālū arjih wa-akhāhu wa-ib'ʿath fī l-madāini ḥāshirīna

tr.85: They answered, ‘Delay him and his brother for a while, and send messengers to all the cities
tr.19: They said: Put him off, (him) and his brother, and send into the cities summoners
tr.22: They said: "Keep him and his brother in suspense (for a while), and dispatch to the Cities heralds to collect-
tr.203: They said: "Put him off and his brother (for a while), and send callers to the cities;

26.en: Who will bring you every learned, skilled magician."

tr.85: to bring every accomplished sorcerer to you.’
tr.19: Who shall bring unto thee every knowing wizard.
tr.22: "And bring up to thee all (our) sorcerers well-versed."
tr.203: "To bring up to you every well-versed sorcerer."

26.en: So the magicians were assembled for the appointment of a well-known day.

tr.85: The sorcerers were [to be] assembled at the appointed time on a certain day
tr.19: So the wizards were gathered together at a set time on a day appointed.
tr.22: So the sorcerers were got together for the appointment of a day well-known,
tr.203: So the sorcerers were assembled at a fixed time on a day appointed.

26.en: And it was said to the people, "Will you congregate.

tr.85: and the people were asked, "Are you all coming?
tr.19: And it was said unto the people: Are ye (also) gathering?
tr.22: And the people were told: "Are ye (now) assembled?-
tr.203: And it was said to the people: "Are you (too) going to assemble?

26.ar: لَعَلَّنَا نَتَّبِعُ ٱلسَّحَرَةَ إِن كَانُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلْغَـٰلِبِينَ
26.en: That we might follow the magicians if they are the predominant?"
26.tl: laʿallanā nattabiʿu l-saḥarata in kānū humu l-ghālibīna

tr.85: We may follow the sorcerers if they win!"
tr.19: (They said): Aye, so that we may follow the wizards if they are the winners.
tr.22: "That we may follow the sorcerers (in religion) if they win?"
tr.203: "That we may follow the sorcerers [who were on Fir‘aun’s (Pharaoh) religion of disbelief] if they are the winners."

26.ar: فَلَمَّا جَآءَ ٱلسَّحَرَةُ قَالُوا۟ لِفِرْعَوْنَ أَئِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجْرًا إِن كُنَّا نَحْنُ ٱلْغَـٰلِبِينَ
26.en: And when the magicians arrived, they said to Pharaoh, "Is there indeed for us a reward if we are the predominant?"
26.tl: falammā jāa l-saḥaratu qālū lifir'ʿawna a-inna lanā la-ajran in kunnā naḥnu l-ghālibīna

tr.85: When the sorcerers came, they said to Pharaoh, ‘Shall we be rewarded if we win?’
tr.19: And when the wizards came they said unto Pharaoh: Will there surely be a reward for us if we are the winners?
tr.22: So when the sorcerers arrived, they said to Pharaoh: "Of course - shall we have a (suitable) reward if we win?
tr.203: So when the sorcerers arrived, they said to Fir‘aun (Pharaoh): "Will there surely be a reward for us if we are the winners?"

26.ar: قَالَ نَعَمْ وَإِنَّكُمْ إِذًا لَّمِنَ ٱلْمُقَرَّبِينَ
26.en: He said, "Yes, and indeed, you will then be of those near [to me]."
26.tl: qāla naʿam wa-innakum idhan lamina l-muqarabīna

tr.85: and he said, ‘Yes, and you will join my inner court.’
tr.19: He said: Aye, and ye will then surely be of those brought near (to me).
tr.22: He said: "Yea, (and more),- for ye shall in that case be (raised to posts) nearest (to my person)."
tr.203: He said: "Yes, and you shall then verily be of those brought near (to myself)."

26.ar: قَالَ لَهُم مُّوسَىٰٓ أَلْقُوا۟ مَآ أَنتُم مُّلْقُونَ
26.en: Moses said to them, "Throw whatever you will throw."
26.tl: qāla lahum mūsā alqū mā antum mul'qūna

tr.85: Moses said to them, ‘Throw down whatever you will.’
tr.19: Moses said unto them: Throw what ye are going to throw!
tr.22: Moses said to them: "Throw ye - that which ye are about to throw!"
tr.203: Mûsâ (Moses) said to them: "Throw what you are going to throw!"

26.ar: فَأَلْقَوْا۟ حِبَالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقَالُوا۟ بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلْغَـٰلِبُونَ
26.en: So they threw their ropes and their staffs and said, "By the might of Pharaoh, indeed it is we who are predominant."
26.tl: fa-alqaw ḥibālahum waʿiṣiyyahum waqālū biʿizzati fir'ʿawna innā lanaḥnu l-ghālibūna

tr.85: They threw their ropes and staffs, saying, ‘By Pharaoh’s might, we shall be victorious.’
tr.19: Then they threw down their cords and their staves and said: By Pharaoh's might, lo! we verily are the winners.
tr.22: So they threw their ropes and their rods, and said: "By the might of Pharaoh, it is we who will certainly win!"
tr.203: So they threw their ropes and their sticks, and said: "By the might of Fir‘aun (Pharaoh), it is we who will certainly win!"

26.ar: فَأَلْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِىَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ
26.en: Then Moses threw his staff, and at once it devoured what they falsified.
26.tl: fa-alqā mūsā ʿaṣāhu fa-idhā hiya talqafu mā yafikūna

tr.85: But Moses threw his staff and- lo and behold!- it swallowed up their trickery
tr.19: Then Moses threw his staff and lo! it swallowed that which they did falsely show.
tr.22: Then Moses threw his rod, when, behold, it straightway swallows up all the falsehoods which they fake!
tr.203: Then Mûsâ (Moses) threw his stick, and behold, it swallowed up all that they falsely showed!

26.en: So the magicians fell down in prostration [to Allāh].

tr.85: and the sorcerers fell down on their knees,
tr.19: And the wizards were flung prostrate,
tr.22: Then did the sorcerers fall down, prostrate in adoration,
tr.203: And the sorcerers fell down prostrate.

26.en: They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds,

tr.85: exclaiming, ‘We believe in the Lord of the Worlds,
tr.19: Crying: We believe in the Lord of the Worlds,
tr.22: Saying: "We believe in the Lord of the Worlds,
tr.203: Saying: "We believe in the Lord of the ‘Âlamîn (mankind, jinn and all that exists).

26.en: The Lord of Moses and Aaron."

tr.85: the Lord of Moses and Aaron.’
tr.19: The Lord of Moses and Aaron.
tr.22: "The Lord of Moses and Aaron."
tr.203: "The Lord of Mûsâ (Moses) and Hârûn (Aaron)."
